Від HOLYSTUDIO

Як користуватися гайдом

Ми підготували для вас свіжий розбір роботи з Higgsfield: як створити ультрареалістичний AI-фільм — від одного фото й розробки персонажа до локацій, бійок, діалогів та VFX.

Спеціально для вас ми переклали матеріал і зібрали пояснення, промпти, референси та відеоприклади в одному місці, щоб ви могли легко пройти весь процес і застосувати ці прийоми у власних проєктах.

Цей гайд доповнює уроки, які ви вже пройшли, та знайомить вас із найновішими підходами до AI-відеопродакшену на прикладі реального фільму.

  • Промпти — англійською, як в оригіналі. Кнопка «Скопіювати промпт» забирає текст повністю, навіть якщо він згорнутий.
  • Бейджі над промптом показують модель, формат кадру, роздільність і тривалість.
  • Теги на кшталт @char_adam_video_v1 — назви елементів. Створи свої елементи з такими самими назвами або заміни теги на свої.
  • Зміст — кнопка внизу праворуч, щоб швидко перейти до потрібної сцени.
01
01 Підготовка

Перед стартом

Створи персонажів, локації та реквізит як Elements (елементи). Для Адама, Рона й Віктора використовуй відео-елементи; назви в Claude і Higgsfield мають бути однаковими. Рана Віктора — окремий референс-зображення.

02
02 Скіли для Claude

Скіли, на яких тримається воркфлоу

Розкажи Claude, що відбувається, — а скіли перетворять твою режисуру на відеопромпти. Скіл сцени — для кадрів, скіл бійки — для хореографії, скіл акторської гри — для перформансу.

01Скіл сцени
higgsfield-prompt-engine.skill

Драматургія сцени

П’ятиелементний «двигун» сцени: Мета, Перешкода, Тактика, Поворот, Зміна цінності. Пише сцени й секвенції та перевіряє їх на структурну силу.

Коли вмикати: Коли треба написати сцену, дати варіанти або зрозуміти, чому сцена «не працює».

02Скіл бійки
higgsfield-fight-scene.skill

Хореографія бійок

Хореограф бійок у стилі Jeet Kune Do (та Wing Chun): стійки, удари, стоп-хіти, низькі кіки, реакції на удар — розписано по бітах із таймінгом і цілями, готово для вставки в промпт.

Коли вмикати: Будь-яка бійка, сутичка чи екшн-секвенція. Архів містить 56 файлів-довідників — завантажуй його цілим.

03Скіл акторської гри
higgsfield-acting-skill.skill

Жива акторська гра

Метод для блоків ACTING TASK: мета сцени, мотив кожного персонажа, задача для очей. Робить AI-акторів живими, а не «скляними».

Коли вмикати: Діалоги, емоційні біти, реакції, «мертві» очі або переграш.

04Скіл оптики
Anamorphic skill.md

Анаморфний вигляд

Пише блок анаморфної оптики для промптів: вибір фокусної відстані, овальне боке, горизонтальні флери, розмиття, плівка. Модель слухається не назви об’єктива, а візуальних ознак.

Коли вмикати: Локації (24–35 мм), портрети (85 мм), будь-який «film still» — щоб не прописувати оптику щоразу вручну.

Як встановити скіл у Claude
  1. Увімкни виконання коду. Settings → Capabilities → «Create and edit files». Без цього скіли не працюють.
  2. Відкрий скіли. Customize → Skills (адреса claude.ai/customize/skills).
  3. Завантаж архів. «+» → «Create skill» → «Upload a skill» → обери завантажений .zip. Архів не розпаковуй.
  4. Увімкни й працюй. Скіл з’явиться у списку — перемкни його в On. Далі просто опиши сцену в чаті: Claude сам підхопить потрібний скіл, або назви його прямо — «використай higgsfield-acting-skill».

Якщо завантаження не стартує у твоєму вікні — натисни «Скопіювати SKILL.md» і встав текст у новий скіл чи в інструкції проєкту Claude, або скачай файли з оригінального гайду на Higgsfield ↗.

04
04 Бонус HOLYSTUDIO

Лайфхаки
з відеорозбору

Ми спеціально зібрали важливі поради з відео окремо в одному місці. Натисни таймкод, щоб відкрити потрібний момент на YouTube.

▶ 1:06

Порядок у проєкті

У Cinema Studio — окрема папка на кожну сцену, всередині підпапки для персонажів, локацій і реквізиту. Пів хвилини на старті економлять години пошуку потім.

▶ 2:06

Текстури як у 3D

Пластикова шкіра й «мертве» волосся після GPT Image прибираються окремими референсами на волосся, шкіру, тканину й фон — і для кожного прямо пишеш, що з нього взяти.

▶ 3:45

Відео-елемент замість фото

Фото показує, як персонаж виглядає. Відео — ще й як рухається обличчя і як він звучить. Гра природніша, менше кредитів на дублі з «чужим» обличчям. Для голосу вистачить простого запису на кшталт «This is how I look and this is how I sound».

▶ 4:51

Оптика живе в референсі

24 мм анаморф — для локацій, 35 мм — щільніший кадр. М’якший фон відокремлює героя, і цей вигляд переходить із референсу локації у відео. Щоб не писати оптику щоразу — Anamorphic skill.

▶ 6:10

Однакові назви — в Claude і Higgsfield

Збережи кожен асет як елемент і дай Claude ту саму назву. Тоді промпт із тегом сам підтягне потрібний елемент. А скіл не замінює режисуру: опиши, як наростає емоція, хто що кричить і куди йде камера.

▶ 7:01

Чернетки в 480p і батчі

На першому проході дивишся тільки кадрування й розстановку — генеруй у 480p. Переможців перегенеровуй у 1080p. Той самий промпт дає різні дублі, і випадковий може подарувати кілер-кадр.

▶ 10:12

Бійка — списком

Пиши бійку як список: хто де стоїть, що робить герой, як падає кожен суперник. Середні плани показують рух, крупні продають контакт. У складних місцях — куди йде стопа і в який бік падають.

▶ 11:46

Склейки на русі

Швидка панорама (whip pan) — ідеальне місце, щоб сховати склейку. Чотири дублі — одна бійка без видимих швів.

▶ 12:15

Relight замість нового ролу

Кімната подобається, а настрій ні — не перегенеровуй, а перевисвіти. Для діалогу зроби другу сторону тієї ж кімнати: диван за Віктором, двері за Адамом — і модель завжди знає, куди дивиться.

▶ 12:44

Два правила діалогу

Репліки — слово в слово, інакше модель перепише сценарій. І не плануй кожен кадр: дай правила камери, а шот-лист побудує скіл. Порада для монтажу: повторюй останню репліку попередньої генерації — буде нахлест, де різати.

▶ 14:43

VFX — через конкретні референси

Куля виглядала як металева кулька й міняла форму. Рішення: фото стріляної кулі, фото рани потрібного розміру і чіткий порядок — куля виходить, падає, рана видима, доки камера не сховає Віктора.

▶ 15:20

Блокінг і нові ракурси

Для бійки зменш сцену до 2 м біля дивана. Зроби з фото локації коротку «екскурсію кімнатою», візьми кадр згори й познач стартові позиції. А один вдалий дубль можна перезняти з інших ракурсів, подавши його як відеореференс.

05
05 Етап 1

Етап 1 — Створюємо асети

Адам — від фото до персонажа

Адам почався з фото автора: біле волосся, бліда шкіра, атлетична статура, довгий чорний шкіряний плащ і срібні аксесуари. Автор протестував кучеряве й пряме волосся, зберігаючи костюм і макет карточки незмінними.

Що це дає: дві альтернативні карточки дизайну з одного фото. Це вхідні матеріали для дизайну; багаторазовий референс для сцен — це відео-елемент, зроблений із затвердженого персонажа.

Що це дає: карточка Адама з кучерявим волоссям — обличчя, костюм і двопанельний макет лишаються незмінними.

Palette of 70% black leather and washed-black cotton, 18% cool neutral grey backdrop, 12% pale white skin, white hair, the white belt and polished silver as the brightest values in the frame. Cinematic film still texture with fine organic grain, true-to-life proportions, no visible logos, patches or text, no captions or labels on the sheet.

Додаємо реальну текстуру

Що це дає: окремі референси для волосся, шкіри, фону й текстури футболки.

Віктор — кастинг антагоніста

Що це дає: фіксує людську зовнішність Віктора до того, як з неї буде створено багаторазовий відео-елемент.

Для Віктора автор переглянув варіанти в AI Cast і обрав обличчя, яке підходить під роль. Обраний кадр стає відправною точкою для його людського відео-елемента.

Кастинг: чоловік, близько 45 років, високий, бурштинові очі, коротке хвилясте сиве волосся, борода, формальний одяг.

Сцена 1.1 — Телефонний дзвінок

Що це дає: запускає історію: Рон втрачає самовладання, Адам кладе слухавку на півслові й їде геть.

Один промпт — чотири корисні дублі. Залиш вступ Адама, гру Рона, момент зі слухавкою та від'їзд — і змонтуй їх разом.

Промпт 11· Відео
Seedance 2.521:91080p30 с
SCENE CONTEXT
Block 1 of 6. Thirty seconds, 21:9. One call already in progress across two spaces. Ron has lost one of his own and is sending Adam after the killer. He starts holding himself together and comes apart in stages—nerves, simmer, boil, break. Adam listens, takes what he needs from the call, hangs up, and leaves. Gritty neo-noir, night.
ACTIVE REFERENCES
@char_ron_video_v1 — VIDEO ELEMENT — RON. Face, grey hair, hands, and wardrobe match the reference. VOICE: use the voice heard in this reference—the same timbre, low rough register, rasp, and breath—through every line, from nervous speech to the full scream. The scream is that same voice pushed to breaking. Ron holds a cigarette in his LEFT hand and a black corded receiver in his RIGHT hand. The reference controls identity and voice; pose, props, and lighting come from this prompt.
@char_adam_video_v1 — VIDEO ELEMENT — ADAM. Build, jacket, thin silver chain at the collar, and hands match the reference. Adam is seen only as a silhouette from behind, a hand, and a back. His face stays out of every frame. The reference controls appearance; Adam remains silent.
@loc_room_ron_v1 — RON’S OFFICE. Controls layout, materials, and practical lighting: a heavy wooden table, a warm table lamp, a glass ashtray, and a black landline base with a coiled cord. The reference’s camera angle and framing are not inherited.
@loc_alley_v1 — THE ALLEY. Controls layout and materials: wet asphalt, brick walls, a weak sodium lamp in the distance, and an old glass-and-steel booth against the left wall. Inside the booth is a smooth matte-black wall-mounted box with a steel cradle hook and a heavy black receiver on a cord. The reference’s camera angle and framing are not inherited.
@prop_bike — ADAM’S MOTORCYCLE with rear case. Controls the bike’s appearance.
LOCATION MAP
Room: the table runs left–right across the frame. Ron sits at the near long side, body turned three-quarters toward camera-right. The lamp is at the left end of the table; the ashtray and landline base are within reach. The camera works from Ron’s right side throughout.
Alley: a narrow corridor running away from the camera toward the distant sodium lamp. The booth stands against the left wall in the near depth, its doorway open toward the alley. @prop_bike is parked against the same wall about three metres beyond the booth, pointing down the alley. The camera works from behind and camera-right of Adam. His direction of travel is away from the camera into depth.
FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
Open in Ron’s office. Extreme close-up of Ron’s mouth, jaw, and the receiver, viewed three-quarters from his right, with the camera rolled 15°. The receiver is already at his right ear, its lower mouthpiece beside his lips. He is already speaking.
Adam is already inside the booth in the alley, facing the wall-mounted box, with the receiver at his right ear and a cigarette in his left hand. His back faces the alley. The bike is parked farther along the wall. Exactly one person is present in each location.
FORMAT MODE
Controlled multi-shot sequence, 30 seconds, hard cuts. Each segment below specifies its opening frame.
OPTICS
Close-ups: 47° diagonal field of view, with a natural perspective.
Table medium-wide: 63° diagonal field of view.
Final alley wide: 84° diagonal field of view, classic wide rectilinear perspective.
Keep the lens fixed within each shot. Gentle horizontal flares may appear around practical lights.
CAMERA
Dialogue and stillness use a tripod or one slow, controlled move. Ron’s outburst is filmed on a locked-off tripod so his physical movement drives the shot. Adam’s departure uses a static, low camera, with the bike moving away into depth.
ACTION TIMING
0–5s — SHOT 1 — @loc_room_ron_v1.
Extreme close-up from just below Ron’s mouth, three-quarters from his right. Roll the camera 15° so the lamp light cuts diagonally across the frame. Show his mouth, jaw edge, and receiver against his right cheek. His lips are dry. He speaks quickly, with an unsteady breath between words, trying to sound in control.
RON: “This goddamn puppy need to learn its own place.”
His cigarette hand briefly enters the edge of the frame. Hard cut.
5–9s — SHOT 2 — @loc_alley_v1.
Tight close-up from behind Adam. Place the camera about 0.3 metres above the wet ground, just inside the open booth doorway and slightly to his right, aimed steeply up his back. Roll the camera 15°.
His dark shoulders, jacket collar, and receiver at his right ear fill the frame. A small glint catches the chain at his collar. The booth’s steel frame and glass close the shot on both sides, with only a sliver of wet street visible below.
Slowly push in toward his shoulders. His cigarette stays low in his left hand; a little smoke curls past his shoulder. His face remains hidden.
Through the receiver, Ron speaks lower, almost to himself. His voice is thin and filtered but recognisably the voice from @char_ron_video_v1.
RON: “I knew the things would go south…”
A swallow from Ron. Adam stays still. Hard cut.
9–12s — SHOT 3 — @loc_room_ron_v1.
Level medium-wide shot on a tripod, from Ron’s right-side three-quarter angle. The table runs across the lower frame, lamp on the left, ashtray and landline base within reach.
Ron leans back with the receiver at his ear. His cigarette hand jabs the air twice, then drops to the table. His fingers drum once, stop, and spread flat. He is trying to contain the anger.
Then he sits forward in one motion, chest thrust toward the desk, mouth wide. He screams the name at full voice.
RON: “NOW THEY KILLED KENNY!”
His voice tears on “Kenny.” A few drops of saliva catch the lamp light.
12–16s — SHOT 3 CONTINUES.
Ron rises out of the chair and leans over the table. He moves the receiver away from his ear and holds it upright in front of his face: the earpiece points upward, and the lower mouthpiece sits a few centimetres from his lips.
He shouts directly into that lower mouthpiece. The cord pulls taut. His left fist, still holding the cigarette, hits the wood on the final word. The ashtray jumps and spins, ash scatters, the lampshade shivers, and the cigarette snaps in his fingers.
RON: “I NEED THIS DOG'S HEAD ON MY TABLE!!!”
His voice is hoarse and cracks on “table.” A little saliva catches on his lower lip and the mouthpiece. He stays bent over the desk, breathing hard through his nose.
Hard cut as the next line begins.
16–18s — SHOT 4 — @loc_alley_v1.
Extreme close-up from behind and camera-right of Adam, at a three-quarter angle. Frame his right hand, the heavy black receiver, and the steel cradle hook directly below it. These fill the frame. Everything behind them is dark matte black and out of focus. His shoulder cuts the edge of the shot; his head remains above frame.
From the receiver, tiny and distorted:
RON: “This piece of sh—”
Adam slams the receiver onto the hook mid-word. One hard metal clack. Ron’s voice stops immediately.
Cut on the clack.
18–20s — SHOT 5 — @loc_alley_v1.

SCENE CONTEXT
Thirty-second multi-shot sequence. A lone man walks into a packed industrial nightclub: seen from high above, the camera behind him, he takes his first steps and slides through a crowd that is dancing and having fun — through gaps the dance itself opens, touching nobody — while the camera sinks slowly toward him with the horizon tilted; then, in slow motion at his side, he moves past people staring hard at every face; then the crowd itself becomes the foreground and we see him through it. One story beat: the hunter enters a room that is dancing.

Physics: weight shifts foot to foot on every move, hips and shoulders carry it, hair and loose clothes lag a moment behind each move and fan out on every turn, drinks slosh and spill over knuckles, sweat shines on necks and temples, hair sticks to foreheads; bodies sway and part and close again like a rough sea, and when two dancers brush shoulders they sway, laugh and dance on. Сцена 2.5 — Охорона помічає Адама

Що це дає: вечірка перетворюється на загрозу. Старший охоронець віддає наказ «Kill him» («Убий його»), а крупний план кийка робить небезпеку відчутною.

Промпт 18· Відео
Seedance 2.521:91080p30 с
SCENE CONTEXT
Thirty-second multi-shot sequence, nine shots, an alternative opening for the guards' beat. It opens in real time tight on the DJ's hands working the decks — a fader shoved up, a knob cranked, switches flicked — then his face over the mixer, then his arm thrown out to the crowd in a big wave; then a crane pulls back from him out over the dancing crowd, and the crowd plays in slow motion — thirteen seconds of the club at its peak. Then, back in real time, a close-up of the senior guard with the other two standing to his right; he speaks to the second guard, the focus pulls to the second guard as the order reaches him — "Kill him." — and in an extreme close-up the second guard tests his electric baton — on, one crackle, off. He walks into the crowd with it dark at his thigh.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@char_dj_image_v1 — the DJ: a Black man with a short cropped fade, a thin mustache and a small goatee, dark aviator sunglasses in thin metal frames, big silver-and-black over-ear headphones on a black cable, a plain black crew-neck T-shirt and one thin silver chain — 100% matches the reference. Behind the decks in the raised booth at the far end in big headphones, working the mixer and hyping the crowd the whole time: hands on the faders, knobs and switches of the mixer, head hammering down again and again, body bouncing, one arm thrown out over the rail and waving to the crowd. He never leaves the booth; he is seen, not heard.
@char_club_guard_1_image_v1 — Guard 1, the senior: the biggest and heaviest of the three, heavy stern face, short slicked hair, black suit over a black shirt, leather-soled shoes — 100% matches the reference. He spots Adam, points, gives the order, leads the run. He gives the order.
@char_club_guard_2_image_v1 — Guard 2: lean, sharp cheekbones, hair combed back, black suit over a black shirt — 100% matches the reference. Stands on Guard 1's right. He receives the order, tests his baton and walks into the crowd with it dark at his thigh.
@char_club_guard_3_image_v1 — Guard 3, the youngest and fastest: smooth face, neat dark hair, black suit over a black shirt — 100% matches the reference. Runs on Guard 1's right; the fastest. Stands at the far end of the row, beside Guard 2.
@prop_electric_baton — one per guard, all three identical and 100% matching the reference: a stun baton about 55 cm long: a black ribbed rubber grip with a wrist-strap loop at the butt end and a round black hand guard at the front; on top of the grip just behind the guard, a small switch and a red indicator dot; the shaft a row of worn, scuffed chrome steel rings with thin black gaps between them; a black end cap with two short steel prongs sticking straight out of it. It is a contact weapon. The reference shows it switched off — dark and silent, the rings dull steel — and it stays that way until a shot switches it on: the thumb presses the small switch on top of the grip, the red indicator dot beside it lights up, and while the switch is held on, bright blue-white sparks jump between the prongs and along the rings with a loud dry crackle; pressed against bare skin the sparks vanish and the crackle drops to a muffled buzz — a half-second touch is a stinging jolt and a local cramp, it never throws anyone and never knocks anyone out. Thick leather does not conduct: pressed against leather the sparks keep crawling and snapping on its surface and nothing passes through. The instant it leaves the hand it goes dark and silent. The crane move is smooth and continuous; the roll of the frame stays level. The baton sparks only while the switch is held; the moment the thumb lifts it goes dark. It is carried low along the thigh, prongs to the floor, never on the shoulder or against the body. Dancers are never touched. Fire and strobe follow the locked rhythm.

The light in every shot is the light of @loc_club_dancefloor_v1 exactly as it is in the reference image — the same sources in the same places, with the same colour, direction and brightness, and the same darkness between them — copied as it is. Faces and bodies receive only what that light gives them where they stand; a face standing in the dark stays dark. The only two changes to it are the locked strobe frame every 3 seconds and the fire cannon every 5 seconds described in SHOW RHYTHM.

Sound effects only, diegetic — voices, feet, glass, fire, strobe, baton; the DJ is seen, not heard. Shots 1–4: the roar of a packed hall, shouts and whistles, hundreds of feet on wet concrete; in shot 1 the small clicks of switches and the slide of a fader close to the mic under the roar; in the slow-motion shot the room sound stretches low and heavy. Shots 5–9: the room pulled back; shot 6: one voice, the senior guard's, in English, exactly "Kill him.", low and flat — the only words in the sequence; shot 8: the click of the switch, the dry crackle of the sparks, a second click and the crackle gone; shot 9: only the crowd — no crackle. The whoosh of a fire cannon every 5 seconds and the dry tick of the strobe every 3 seconds. No narration, no subtitles.

Photoreal crime-drama texture, anamorphic cinema look, the energy of the club at its peak cut against a quiet, tense order, the location's own colour exactly as in the reference, fine film grain.
QUALITY
Faces sharp where they are the subject; the DJ's hands and the mixer sharp and correctly shaped in shot 1; the crane move in shot 4 smooth and continuous; the focus pull in shot 6 smooth and deliberate; lips in sync with the two words in shot 6; the DJ, three distinct guards, no merged bodies; the baton correctly shaped, sparking only while live and in hand; stable cadence across nine shots. SCENE CONTEXT
Thirty-second multi-shot sequence, real time, twenty-one shots, cut like a fight montage. It opens on a crane shot that starts straight above Adam — a top shot into a packed dancing crowd with three black suits cutting three lines through the heads toward him from three sides — and sinks and swings down in one move until it ends on his face. Then the three guards reach him at once, from the left, from the right and from behind, and he takes them one at a time, fast, exact and sharp — a pivot, a pin, a duck, and short straight strikes that go out and back in a quarter of a second — until all three are on the wet concrete around his boots. He goes still, pushes his hair back with one hand, settles his coat, and walks out of frame into the dancers. The strobe fires every three seconds for the whole thirty, locked to the clock; a fire cannon every five.

PLAYABLE INTENTIONS
Adam is standing inside the crowd, and three men are coming for him at once from three sides; that is the obstacle, and the tactic is the oldest one: do not fight three, fight one three times — move so that only one of them can reach him at a time, and finish each before the next arrives. Nothing he does is wide or angry: every answer is the shortest line, out and back, and between answers he is completely still. The guards want it quick and ugly and all at once; each one arrives a half-beat apart, and each one is alone when he gets there. The audience's read: three armed men were never a fight, and he knew it before they did. At the end he pushes his hair back — the one human, careless gesture in the block — and walks off as if he had been dancing. Adam's face shows only the jaw, the nostrils and the vein at his temple. The crowd wants its night and never stops dancing.

THE CROWD — DANCING PACKED TIGHT, NEVER SCATTERING, NOT CARING
The crowd is ordinary club-goers in all kinds of different everyday and party clothes and colours — a white shirt, a red dress, a denim jacket, a yellow top, a striped tee, a green bomber, a silver sequin dress, a grey hoodie, a pink blouse, bare shoulders, a leather jacket, a baseball cap — young men and women of every look; only the guards wear black suits. Nobody in the crowd stands still for a single frame: they dance packed tight shoulder to shoulder, and every person moves hard in their own way — one girl whips her long hair in circles, a guy jumps straight up again and again, a couple grinds pressed together, a girl rolls her hips with her arms straight up, two friends bounce shoulder to shoulder, someone spins, someone drinks from a bottle mid-dance, someone films the DJ with a phone held high, arms go up in ragged waves. The crowd never forms a ring, a circle or an audience around anyone — nobody stands watching with a drink like a spectator, nobody faces the fight on purpose — it never scatters, and it does not care: they laugh, sing, jump, drink and dance, sway around three men on the floor without a glance, and let the guards and Adam squeeze between them without noticing. Nobody in the crowd is ever touched: no blow, no baton, no falling body reaches a club-goer — the dancers nearest a swing or a fall sway a half-step clear and dance on. The packed dancing crowd is visible in every shot, and nobody looks into the lens. CAMERA LANGUAGE
Shot 1 is one continuous crane move: it starts aimed straight down at the floor from about 7 m directly above Adam, sinks and swings round in one smooth, even move, and ends at about 1.2 m from his face at a three-quarter angle, slightly above his eye line — top shot to close-up in one breath, no stops, no speed changes. From shot 2 on, every shot is raw handheld from an operator inside the crowd, bumped by dancers: hard shake, the horizon rocking up to ten degrees, whip pans to whatever moves fastest with focus catching up late. In the fight, shots 4–16, the shake is at its maximum: the frame jerks several times a second, smeared with motion blur, the horizon swinging up to fifteen degrees, as if the operator is being shoved inside the fight. IMPACT JOLT: at the exact frame each contact lands the whole frame kicks hard several degrees in the direction of the force, then shakes on. CAMERA CHASES THE BLOW: on every contact the operator lunges one or two steps in along its line and arrives tight on the point of contact at the instant it lands — the chin, the knee, the nose, the jaw, the neck, the mouth, the sternum — then is already moving to the next target. Every shot of Adam is a three-quarter angle; the top shot looks straight down on him with his shoulders turned at a three-quarter angle to the frame. The strobe does the rest of the style: the decisive frames are frozen razor-sharp for one frame and gone.

SPEED — FAST, EXACT, SHARP
Every strike Adam throws is a snap: it leaves guard, lands and is back inside a quarter of a second; the first visible motion of the limb IS the strike itself, launched from where the hand or foot already rests, with no draw-back and no wind-up; a combination is three to four snaps a second. Every strike names its limb, its striking surface and its exact target and lands exactly there at full speed with no glancing contact; the frame of contact is crisp — knuckles, elbow, heel or the bottom of the fist visibly pressed into the named spot — and the fist is already back at guard while the man is still moving from the hit. Between exchanges Adam is completely still in his narrow side-on stance: the fight is short straight lines and long stillness. Natural 180-degree shutter action cadence: fast strikes and evasions carry brief directional motion blur, then resolve into sharp readable impact poses; no slow motion, no ghosting, no duplicated limbs, no frame-skipping stutter.

FULL CONTACT — A REAL FIGHT
This is a real, brutal fight, not a staged dance. Every action makes full, solid contact: at the frame of impact the knuckles are visibly pressed into the chin, the nose, the mouth; the heel is visibly driven into the side of the knee and into the sternum; the point of the elbow visibly crosses the jaw; the bottom of the fist visibly lands on the back of the neck. Bodies deform at the point of contact, heads are driven along the line of the force, sweat and spit spray. Skin stays clean and unbroken the whole time — every impact shows only the dent, the snap, the sweat and the spit. No blood anywhere in the block. Each decisive contact gets its own tight insert.

MONTAGE
Cut like a real action montage: twenty-one hard cuts in thirty seconds. The opening crane holds for six seconds; every shot inside the fight is under one and a half seconds and most are under one; every other shot is two seconds or shorter. In the fight every cut lands on an impact or on the start of a move, and each decisive contact is shown twice — the move in a medium shot, then the hit in a tight insert — match-cut on the direction of the force. The three fights overlap by a half-beat: as one man goes down the next is already swinging. The block opens from above and ends with the crowd closing behind him.

FORMAT MODE
Anamorphic 2.39:1. Real time throughout, no slow motion anywhere. Hard cuts, no dissolves.

OPTICS
Anamorphic look, lens wide open: very shallow depth of field, only the subject's plane sharp, heavy creamy blur with horizontal oval anamorphic bokeh. 35mm (about 63° diagonal FOV) for the crane, full bodies, legs and the crowd, 50mm (about 47°) for medium shots, 85mm (about 29°) for faces, hands and inserts. Lens locked inside each shot.

PHYSICS
The crowd dances on and is never touched; every swing, fall and body stays inside the body-wide gap between dancers, who sway a half-step clear and dance on. Wet concrete: soles skid, bodies slide, a falling man splashes. A guard's baton is dark until the strike: the thumb presses the momentary switch as the swing starts, so the sparks are born in the first hand's-width of the swing and the crackle starts with it; the instant the fingers open it goes dark and it clatters and bounces once on its rings. A pivot on the lead foot turns the body a quarter turn in a fraction of a second and fans the long coat out flat; a full-weight overhead chop that misses drags the swinger past his target. A straight fist into the point of the chin snaps the head straight back and clacks the teeth; the fist is back at guard while the man still staggers. A heel stamped into the side of a loaded knee folds the joint inward and the man pitches forward onto his front. A palm that slaps a thrusting forearm down and inward pins the arm across the attacker's own body and leaves his face open in the same beat; a straight fist into the nose flattens it and snaps the head back. A hard yank on the wrist down past the hip drags the man forward and down into the elbow coming the other way; an elbow across the jaw whips the head sideways and springs the fingers open. A fist dropped like a hammer on the back of a bowed neck puts the man flat on his front. Ducking straight down under a flat swing leaves the swinger's arm wide and his face open. Four vertical fists down one rail in little over a second drive the head back four times and walk a big man backward. A side kick with the heel into the sternum, hip and shoulder stacked behind it, drives a heavy man one step back off his feet and onto his back. The coat whips on every move; between actions Adam is completely still in his narrow side-on stance.

LIGHTING — LOCKED TO THE LOCATION
The light in every shot is the light of @loc_club_dancefloor_v1 exactly as it is in the reference image — the same sources in the same places, with the same colour, direction and brightness, and the same darkness between them — copied as it is. Faces and bodies receive only what that light gives them where they stand; a face standing in the dark stays dark. The only changes to it are the locked strobe frame every 3 seconds, the fire cannon every 5 seconds described in SHOW RHYTHM, and, up close, the blue-white flicker of a baton during the swing it is switched on for.

AUDIO
Sound effects only, diegetic — bodies, voices, glass, fire, strobe, batons; the DJ is seen, not heard; no spoken words. The roar of a packed dancing hall, shouts, whistles and laughter the whole time, hundreds of feet on wet concrete; three sets of steps shoving through bodies; a switch click and a whip-crack of crackle born in a swing, three times in the block; a shaft whistling past an ear, a shaft whistling over a head; the leather coat snapping round on the pivot; the crack of knuckles on a chin and teeth clacking; the crunch of a heel into a knee; a body hitting wet concrete face-first; a palm slapping a forearm and the crack of knuckles on a nose in the same instant; the crack of an elbow on a jaw; the dull thud of a hammer fist on a neck; a second body hitting the floor; four fast cracks of knuckles on a face; the deep thump of a heel on a sternum and the air leaving a big man; a heavy back slamming onto wet concrete and water splashing; three batons clattering dead, one bouncing on its rings; Adam's steady breathing through the nose; the rasp of rings through hair; leather settling on shoulders; the party noise never dropping, swallowing all of it. The whoosh of a fire cannon every 5 seconds and the dry tick of the strobe every 3 seconds. No narration, no subtitles.

STYLE
Photoreal, contemporary Hollywood action texture, anamorphic cinema look, one long descent from above into a face and then a fight seen as a few razor-sharp frozen frames inside a dark moving crowd, the location's own colour exactly as in the reference, fine film grain, deep contrast with protected shadow detail.

QUALITY
Strikes whip-fast, each a short blur resolving into a crisp contact frame, the fist back at guard before the man has finished moving; each baton a single correctly shaped object, sparking only during its own swing and dark at every other moment; all ten strobe frames razor-sharp and on the clock, each one a single frame, none lasting longer, none on the first frame of a shot; the crane move in shot 1 smooth and continuous from straight down to the face with nothing but the crowd in frame; Adam's face sharp where it is the subject and his eyes unchanged from the reference; the three guards' faces unchanged from their references and never confused with each other; skin clean on every face, no blood anywhere; no merged bodies or duplicated limbs; stable cadence across twenty-one shots. Hard cuts, no dissolves.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Named characters: @char_adam_video_v1, @char_club_guard_1_image_v1, @char_club_guard_2_image_v1 and @char_club_guard_3_image_v1 — four men, no other guards, three different guard faces. Everything happens inside a packed dancing crowd with bodies overlapping everyone and no empty floor around anyone. Shot 1 is one continuous crane move from a top shot straight above Adam down and round to a close-up of his face, with three black suits converging on him from three edges of the frame. The three guards reach him at once from screen-left, screen-right and behind, each with a baton that is dark until his own swing; Adam takes them one at a time in this order: @char_club_guard_3_image_v1 from behind — pivot, straight fist to the chin, low sideways kick to the knee, face-down; @char_club_guard_2_image_v1 from screen-right — palm pins the thrust and a straight fist lands in the nose in the same beat, wrist yank into an elbow across the jaw, hammer fist to the back of the neck, face-down; @char_club_guard_1_image_v1 from screen-left — duck under the swing, four straight fists down the centre of the face, heel side kick into the sternum, onto his back. Every baton leaves its owner's hand dark and Adam never touches one. All three stay down. Adam goes completely still, pushes his hair back once with his right hand, settles his coat, and walks out of the right edge of the frame into the dancers; the block ends on the three men on the floor inside the dancing crowd with Adam gone. The crowd is ordinary club-goers in all kinds of different clothes, dancing packed tight the whole time, never standing still, never forming a ring or an audience around anyone, never scattering and not caring; it is visible in every shot and is never touched. Every character is framed at a three-quarter angle; every shot after the crane is handheld; the fight shots are under one and a half seconds each; real time, no slow motion. The strobe fires every 3 seconds on the clock, ten times, locked, never on the first frame of a shot; the fire cannon every 5 seconds, locked; the only other light is the location's own light and the sparks of a baton during its swing. Clean skin on every face and body — impacts show sweat and spit only. Frame 2.39:1 anamorphic.

FIGHT STYLE LOCK: every kick stays below belt height except the one heel into the sternum at waist height; every punch travels a short straight line launched from where the hands already rest at guard — the first visible motion of a limb IS the strike itself; between exchanges the fighter is completely still in his narrow side-on stance; the fight is short straight lines and long stillness.

Cinematic wide interior shot, static camera at chest height, tucked close
to the RIGHT wall of a long corridor and rotated about 30 degrees toward
the left wall — a three-quarter view, deliberately asymmetric: the
corridor runs diagonally from bottom-right toward upper-left, the far end
in the left third of the frame, never centered, converging lines rushing
toward the single door at the end. Shot wide open at T2.0, shallow
anamorphic depth of field with a HEAVY defocused foreground: the focal
plane is a narrow slice resting on the first painting of the left wall
and the lit brass sconce beside it, about 4 meters in — everything nearer
and farther melts fast into deep anamorphic blur.

A dim residential corridor in an aging luxury hotel-apartment building,
15 meters long, 1.8 meters wide, ceiling 2.6 meters, low and heavy, with
NO doors along its walls — the only door is at the far end. Walls above
waist height in dull dark bottle-green wallpaper with a faint tonal
damask, faded unevenly, scuffed paler at hand height, one seam lifting;
below it a tall dado of dark walnut wainscoting with a dulled,
micro-scratched lacquer, heavy walnut rail and skirting. Ceiling painted
brown-black matte with a center row of recessed rectangular warm-white
fluorescent panels behind frosted diffusers every 3 meters, receding in
a shrinking rhythm, two dimmer and yellower, one faintly flickering.
Floor: wall-to-wall dark wool carpet with a small geometric pattern of
tiny squares and diamonds in chocolate-brown, umber and near-black,
crushed paler in a walking line down the middle, a faint stain near the
far end. On the LEFT wall: dark old oil paintings in tarnished gilt and
black-lacquered frames, unevenly spaced, slightly different sizes —
murky landscapes, a still life, a near-black abstract — cracked yellowed
varnish, gilt worn at the corners, one frame hanging crooked; no faces,
no readable text. Small brass sconces with cream half-shades between
them, most OFF, two lit low. At about 7 meters, a narrow walnut console
with a low-lit table lamp under a pleated cream shade and a tall dark
green ceramic floor vase with dry branches. On the RIGHT wall: bare
wallpaper for the first meters, then a long low bench in cracked dark
leather tight against the dado at about 6 meters, and two more dark
paintings beyond it. At the end, 15 meters away, ONE heavy dark walnut
door, flat-paneled, tall brass lever handle and kick plate mottled with
age, brass number UNREADABLE, set slightly off-center right, a thin line
of warm light beneath it. Nothing is perfectly straight — seams drift,
frames hang at different heights, a shade tilts, the bench sits a hand's
width off the wall. Worn, quiet, expensive once — never a clean render.

Foreground, heavily out of focus — surfaces only, nothing in the first
three meters: the near right wall is a thick defocused curtain the camera
shoots through, green wallpaper and walnut dado dissolving into a large
soft dark mass across the right third of the frame, an unlit sconce a
dim oval smear; the first ceiling panel overhead a wide soft warm-white
oval bloom at the top edge; the nearest carpet a soft dark wash along
the bottom.

Midground, in sharp focus: the first painting on the left at about
4 meters — tarnished gilt frame, cracked varnish over a dark landscape,
the lit sconce beside it glowing through its cream shade and pooling
warm light on the green damask and the carved frame edge, the walnut
rail beneath with a long soft sheen, the carpet pattern crisp at its
foot. The only truly sharp zone of the frame.

Background, deeply out of focus: the corridor recedes in oblique
foreshortening into layered dark-green planes, each milkier than the
last; the console lamp a large soft warm oval bloom, the vase a soft
vertical shape; further paintings soft dark rectangles with faint gilt
glints; the bench a low dark mass; the ceiling panels a shrinking
diagonal chain of large stretched warm-white oval highlights; the far
door a tall soft dark mass with a thin warm smear of light at its foot.
No readable shapes, no faces.

Focus falloff is progressive and optical: sharpness lives only on the
focal plane, blur increasing smoothly with distance in both directions,
frame edges and corners noticeably softer than the center, true
large-format shallow-focus depth.

Lighting: cinematic, soft and DARK — underexposed by about a stop and a
half, a true low-key night interior, but with LIFTED SHADOWS: the walls
between panels stay dim but readable, the paintings keep their murky
detail, the carpet keeps its pattern, nothing crushes to pure black, no
shadow pits. Primary: the recessed ceiling panels, warm-white around
3200K, glowing as soft rectangular halos, never visible rays, each
dropping a pool onto the carpet and grazing the frame tops and walnut
dado, pools separated by dim stretches — a receding rhythm of light and
shadow. Accent: two sconces and the console lamp at 2700K, warmer than
the panels, pooling amber on the green wallpaper and catching the gilt —
gentle warm-on-warm contrast. A thin warm line under the far door as the
deepest point of light. NO red, NO magenta, NO colored gels — warm white
and amber only. Specular life only where there is polish: small hard
glints on gilt edges, brass sconces and the far door handle, long soft
sheens down the walnut dado and the cracked leather; the carpet and
matte wallpaper give nothing back. Very faint, barely perceptible haze —
clean air at the camera, thickening gently with distance so the far
panels and the lamp bloom softly and the end sits in a faint milky
glow; no fog, no visible smoke. Heavy natural lens vignette, corners
dark but not black. Controlled highlights, no blown whites on the
diffusers or shades.

Color palette: dull bottle-green and green-black, dark walnut,
chocolate-brown and umber carpet, brown-black ceiling, tarnished gilt,
aged brass, cracked dark leather, warm-white and amber tungsten;
absolutely no red, burgundy or crimson anywhere; no saturated greens, no
neons, no uniform yellow filter, no teal-and-orange wash; blacks
slightly warm and milky; rich low-key contrast, deep velvety textured
shadows, soft rolled-off highlights, gently desaturated — a nocturnal,
romantic-melancholic grade of an old private gallery corridor, faintly
faded like an old print.

Mood: a long dark corridor of old paintings leading to a single closed
door — hushed, heavy, tender and lonely.

Empty location: no people, no characters, no human presence, no
silhouettes, no human shadows, no faces in the paintings. Only the
interior described — no other furniture, no carts, no boxes, no signs,
no readable text, no clutter.

Shot on a REAL 35mm film camera with vintage anamorphic lenses — the
image carries honest optical imperfections of physical glass, not a
digital look.

35mm anamorphic film still. STRONG anamorphic lens character, turned
up to maximum: heavy horizontal squeeze and compression, large
pronounced oval elliptical bokeh, boldly stretched highlights,
curved barrel edge distortion clearly bending straight lines near
the frame edges, visible chromatic aberration fringing toward the
borders.

HEAVY ANAMORPHIC FALLOFF: the focal plane is a narrow slice —
everything off it melts fast and deep. Strong optical softening
claims the outer thirds of the frame: toward the left and right
edges the image smears into thick oval-shaped anamorphic blur, the
corners heavily soft and darkened by natural optical vignetting;
foreground elements near the lens dissolve into large creamy
defocused masses sweeping across the frame; defocused highlights
bloom into big vertical-oval shapes. The falloff is smooth and
optical, never a digital blur overlay or a sharp mask — real
anamorphic glass wide open, melting everything it does not love.

Fine organic 35mm film grain, more visible in the shadows, soft
halation on the brightest highlights — the in-focus sconce, the nearest
ceiling panel, the console lamp, the light under the far door.
Real-world texture: rubbed wallpaper, cracked varnish and worn gilt,
fingerprints on brass, cracked leather, crushed carpet pile — no
plastic surfaces, no clean CGI geometry. NO lens flares, NO light
streaks, NO floating bokeh circles. 2.39:1.
