LOCATION MAP
A long straight corridor, about 30 m long, 2.5 m wide, 3 m high, carpeted, sconces and framed paintings along one wall at eye level, one painting roughly every 4 m; the opposite wall plain. THE RING: 6 m in from the near end the five stand facing each other across the corridor in a loose ring that blocks it — GUARD 4 and GUARD 2 with their backs toward the painting wall, facing across; GUARD 1 and GUARD 5 opposite them with their backs toward the plain wall; GUARD 3 at the far side of the ring, half-turned so one shoulder faces the group and his eyes have the long empty corridor beyond them. ADAM'S ENTRY: the far end, 20 m from the ring; he walks, then runs, toward the ring with the painting wall on his right and the plain wall on his left. THE COLLISION: about 10 m from the ring, where the two runs meet; the fight happens across the width of the corridor there. THE OPERATOR: starts at the near end, 3 m behind the ring, camera in his bare hands at chest height, runs behind the guards, slides along the plain wall on Adam's left for the fight, drops to the carpet among the bodies at 20.5s and stays down there, crawling after Adam, to the cut.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
Handheld, camera in two bare hands at chest height, already shaking hard — a fast jitter and a slow lurch on top of it, in the very first frame — 3 m behind the ring at the near end, angled at three-quarter so the ring sits diagonally: GUARD 4's back and shoulder nearest the lens, half-turned toward the others mid-sentence, GUARD 2 across from him with a hand up, GUARD 1 beside GUARD 2 with his arms folded, GUARD 5 huge at the far side of the ring with his arms hanging, GUARD 3 beyond them half-turned, his face toward the empty corridor. Past the ring the corridor runs away 20 m to the far end, empty. The horizon is already ten degrees off and swinging. Exactly five people in the first frame; six in the scene.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous handheld take, 30 seconds, one camera in one man's bare hands, one lens, one speed ramp into slow motion at 14.5–16.5s and back. The shake is the format, and it is heavy: at no point in the thirty seconds does the frame hold for even a quarter of a second. Two layers of it at all times — a fast fine jitter from the hands, and on top of it a slow heavy lurch from the body — and in the action a third: violent whips that smear the image into streaks, running strides that slam the frame up and down, impacts that throw the whole picture sideways and let it claw back. The horizon swings ten to twenty degrees and is never level. In the slow-motion passage the shake slows with the picture into a wide, heaving, tilted drift that never comes to rest; when the speed snaps back so does the full shake. At the end the camera goes down to the carpet and shakes there — the operator's breathing and his hands on the floor making the low frame tremble and rock — and crawls after Adam shaking. There is no still frame in this take.

OPTICS
One lens for the whole take: 50 mm on full frame, about 47° diagonal — a tight lens for a corridor, which magnifies every tremor of the hands into a visible shudder of the whole picture; the operator gets his close-ups by stepping in and his wides by backing to the wall. Anamorphic character: oval bokeh on the sconces, horizontally stretched highlights, gentle barrel curve at the edges, shallow focus that the operator rides by hand and loses — a beat of soft on every fast refocus, focus breathing under the shake, sconces smeared into streaks on every whip.

CAMERA — one unbroken, violently shaking path
0–4.5s: handheld around the outside of the ring, three-quarter, the frame jittering fast and lurching slow the whole time, sliding half a metre in every direction as the operator shifts his feet, tipping toward whoever is speaking and overshooting him, tilting, faces at mid-shot and never centred for long. 4.5–5.5s: a hard whip-pan off GUARD 3's face down the length of the corridor to Adam — the picture smearing into streaks, overshooting him, jerking back past him, jerking back again, shaking — a beat of soft focus snapping sharp on him, small and walking. 5.5–6.5s: a hard whip-pan straight back to the ring, the picture smearing, landing on all five faces at once in one shaking mid-wide frame as they turn and go ugly together. 6.5–8s: the men break past the lens and knock the camera round with them — a real hit, the picture spinning half a turn and finding them — and the operator runs, the frame slamming up and down with every stride, five backs bouncing ahead under the paintings, and beyond them Adam, running at the lens, closing fast. 8–9.5s: still running, the horizon rocking twenty degrees each way, the operator veering to the plain wall and clipping it — a hard jolt — as Adam leaves the ground and the kick lands in a smear of coat; the frame is thrown. 9.5–14s: the operator slides along the plain wall to Adam's left three-quarter, full bodies in frame, the camera shaking hard from the run and never calming, thrown on every impact — the elbow, the block, the three body shots, the face — and clawing back each time. 14–14.5s: a smearing whip to GUARD 5 as he comes. 14.5–16.5s: the take ramps into slow motion, the shake slowing into a wide heaving tilted drift, the lens at chin height swimming after the lead fist into the jaw. 16.5–19.5s: real speed, the full shake snapping back; the camera drops with Adam's duck, is thrown by the groin shot, dips with the folding man, and is jerked upward by the knee, following the man's head as it snaps back and his body goes over. 19.5–20.5s: the camera trembles and edges around Adam while he stands still. 20.5–23.5s: the operator drops to the carpet — the frame falling, hitting the floor, bouncing — and shoots Adam from the ground, the camera lying on the carpet among the bodies, 15 cm off the floor, tilted up at him, three-quarter from his left and below, his whole figure towering against the ceiling and the sconces, the low frame trembling and rocking with the operator's breathing and his hands on the floor. 23.5–30s: the camera stays on the ground and crawls after Adam as he walks — 20–30 cm off the carpet, bouncing and shaking with the operator's scramble, the bodies passing in the foreground, Adam's boots and coat hem and the backs of his legs ahead, tilted up enough to hold his back and shoulders, dipping as the pistol swings down into frame at his thigh. Every angle a three-quarter or a profile, and no angle holds for a quarter of a second.

ACTION TIMING — stages of one shaking take

0–4.5s — Five men in a ring, killing a shift, the frame jittering and lurching around them. GUARD 4, back to the painting wall, one hand carving the air at the man across from him: 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」 GUARD 2, facing him, takes a half-step in with a hand up: 「『渇き』見ろよ。」 GUARD 1, beside him, arms folded, admits it to the carpet: 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 GUARD 4 laughs at him across the ring. GUARD 5 grunts, unimpressed by all of them, and rolls a shoulder. GUARD 3, at the far side, is not in it: his head is turned, his eyes on the long empty corridor. The camera shudders, tips from speaker to speaker, overshoots each one, never lands square on any of them.

4.5–5.5s — GUARD 3's head stops. Low, flat, to the others: 「おい。」 The camera whips off his face and down the corridor in a smear, overshoots, jerks back: at the far end, small, Adam has walked in and is walking toward them, hands empty at his sides, coat closed, eyes on the ring, the frame shaking around his small figure.

5.5–6.5s — The camera whips straight back to the ring and lands on all five at once, shaking: five heads already turned down the corridor, and in one second the argument is gone from every face and something else is in them — GUARD 2's head pushing forward off his neck and his teeth showing, GUARD 4's grin gone hard, GUARD 1's jaw clenching, GUARD 5's growl coming up out of his chest as his shoulders roll, GUARD 3 already sinking a centimetre into his legs. One beat of five men going ugly together, and they go.

6.5–8s — They break past the lens as a wave, and one of them knocks the camera: the picture spins half a turn, finds the corridor again, shaking. GUARD 2 out in front, a shout tearing out of him; GUARD 4 a step behind him yelling; GUARD 3 low and straight and silent; GUARD 5 heavy and fast a beat later, roaring; GUARD 1 last, running shouting to keep himself running. The operator runs: five backs strung out down the corridor under the paintings, the frame slamming with every stride — and beyond them Adam has broken into a run too, straight at them, coat flying open behind him, closing the twenty metres from both ends.

8–9.5s — Ten metres from the ring the two runs meet, and Adam leaves the ground. Two strides out he launches — the lead knee folding up to his chest in the air and the leg pistoning out sideways, heel leading, hip and shoulder stacked in one straight brace from shoulder to heel — and the flat of his boot slams into GUARD 2's chest and jaw like stamping a heavy door open. GUARD 2 leaves his feet and flies straight back two metres, folding around the boot, and lands flat on his back and does not get up. Adam comes down out of the kick on both feet in the narrow side-on stance, hands already at guard. The camera is thrown by the kick, clips the plain wall with a jolt and comes back shaking.

9.5–11s — GUARD 4 arrives a step behind the first man, arms wide, coming to grab, and gets inside Adam's reach — which is where Adam wants him: chest to chest, Adam's right arm folds and the point of the elbow slices a short flat arc across GUARD 4's jaw, the whole torso turning a few degrees behind it. The head snaps sideways, the grin goes, the legs go, and GUARD 4 drops straight down onto the carpet on his side and does not move. The frame is thrown by the elbow.

11–14s — GUARD 3 arrives low and straight and throws a hard right at Adam's head. Adam's left forearm comes up inside the swing and knocks it a hand's width off its line — the fist glancing past his ear — and he is inside the man's arm. Three short strikes into the body, each one a state already landing, the camera shocked harder on each: a short scooping hook digs up under the floating ribs from a palm's width away, knuckles half-turned up, and the man folds sideways around the spot; his rear fist drives straight through into the solar plexus, hips snapping over, and the man's breath leaves him in a bark and his chin drops; his lead arm bends and hooks tight into the ribs on the other side, elbow staying down, torso turning only a few degrees, and the man's knees dip and his hands come off his guard. Then the fourth: his lead fist fires from exactly where it hovers — one straight line to the chin, knuckles vertical, thumb up, elbow unfolding behind the fist, a short glide-step feeding body weight into it. The head snaps back hard, the man's hands leave his body, and he drops straight down onto the carpet on his back and lies still, the frame lurching down after him and back up to Adam. Adam's hand is already back at guard.

14–16.5s — GUARD 5, the bull, has seen it — three men down in six seconds — and it puts fire in him: he roars and comes at Adam flat out, head down, fists up, huge. The operator lunges in, the frame heaving, and at 14.5s the take ramps into slow motion — the shake slowing with it into a wide, heaving, tilted drift — the lens at chin height from Adam's left at three-quarter: the bull is still a stride out, his right shoulder loading — and in that exact instant Adam's lead fist is already landing on the point of his jaw, the straight line beating the curve, launched from exactly where the hand rested at guard, knuckles vertical, thumb up, elbow unfolding behind the fist, a long glide-step driving his whole body weight down the line of the arm into the running man. The slow motion holds on the contact while the frame swims: the jaw deforms around the knuckles, the lower face pushed across, the eyes rolling up, the head snapping back and up so hard the neck arches and the big shoulders follow it, the run dying under him, his own forward weight doubling the hit. His skin stays clean. Adam's face over his own fist: flat, eyes on the point of contact. At 16.5s the take ramps back to real speed and the full shake snaps back: the bull's knees fold and he goes down rigid, straight back, flat on his back on the carpet with a floor-shaking thud that throws the whole frame, arms out, and does not move.

16.5–19.5s — GUARD 1, the last, arrives shouting and swings a huge wide right at Adam's head — everything he has, eyes half shut for it. Adam's knees fold and his whole body drops a head's height straight down under the arm — the fist passes through the air where his skull was, the camera dropping with him — and from down there, in the same beat, his right fist fires straight up from the guard into GUARD 1's groin, one short vertical line, the knuckles landing with a flat wet thump. Every muscle in GUARD 1 locks at once. A high, breathless sound comes out of him — not a scream, the air leaving — and both his hands clamp between his legs and he folds double, forward, over the pain, his face coming down to the height of Adam's waist. Adam is already rising: both his hands clamp the back of GUARD 1's neck and drag the head down as his right knee drives up — and the knee meets the face with everything Adam's rising body has in it. The head snaps back and up off the knee, the whole folded body straightens with it — upright for one frame, arms flying out from between his legs, eyes already gone — and he goes over backward, stiff, and lands flat on his back on the carpet with a thud that shakes the floor, arms out, out cold. The camera is jerked upward with the knee and follows him over and down, shaking.

19.5–20.5s — Adam settles back into the narrow side-on stance and goes completely still — feet planted, hands frozen at guard, only his eyes tracking over the lead shoulder across the five men on the floor. The stillness is his alone: the camera trembles, breathes and edges sideways around him for the full second, the frame never resting on him.

20.5–23.5s — The operator goes down. The frame drops, hits the carpet, bounces, and comes to lie among the bodies, 15 cm off the floor, tilted up — and there is Adam from the ground: a black figure towering over the lens against the ceiling and the sconces, three-quarter from his left and below, the fallen men's shoulders and boots in the foreground of the low frame, the whole picture trembling and rocking with the operator's breathing on the floor. His hands come down. He takes the coat by both lapels and shakes it out — one hard shake, the black cloth snapping and falling straight — and squares it on his shoulders with one tug and settles the collar, seen from below, huge. One long breath out through the mouth, the shoulders dropping with it, the breath visible in the chest from down here.

23.5–30s — He walks — the same pace he came in with — on down the corridor over the bodies toward where the ring stood, and the camera stays on the ground and scrambles after him: 20–30 cm off the carpet, bouncing hard with the operator's crawl, the fallen men sliding past in the foreground — the sweater flat on his back, the bull's outflung arm, the professional flat, the showman on his side, the hothead flat on his back — Adam's boots and the swinging hem of the coat and the backs of his legs ahead, the frame tilted up enough to hold his back and shoulders, everything shaking. And as he walks, at 26s, his right hand goes up inside the left breast of his coat — above the low frame — and comes back down with the Desert Eagle, the big pistol swinging down into the picture and hanging at his thigh, muzzle down, moving a little with his stride, huge in the low frame, the camera jolting after it along the floor, the paintings and sconces juddering past high above. Hard cut at 30 on his back and the pistol at his side mid-stride, the frame still shaking on the carpet.

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken — all six play it): make it look like nothing. Five men stand in a ring in the middle of a corridor arguing about films because a man at the end of it is nothing; when he turns out to be something they go at him five on one because that is still nothing. Adam plays the same line from his end — he runs at five men because waiting would mean they were something, the fight is a chore, the coat gets shaken out afterward because nothing happened, and the gun comes out only when the corridor is his, for whoever is behind the door. The event is the moment "nothing" turns out to be a very expensive word, and it ends with the one man who never dropped the line walking away down the corridor with the thing he came to use — seen from the floor, where everyone else is.

ACTING TASK — ADAM (fully invested; the work is in his eyes and his stillness):
MOTIVE (his fuel): a man to see at the end of this corridor and a clock running.
GOAL: get past five men spending as little time as possible — and keep the gun for the one who deserves it.
OBSTACLE: five men who want him to stop walking, and a body that wants to enjoy this — the fighter in him wants the bull, and letting him have it costs time.
TACTIC: when they run he runs, because the fastest way through five men is into them, and the first one is close enough to take out of the air. After that each man gets exactly what he brings: the one who comes inside gets the elbow, the one who punches gets a forearm and the body opened up, the one who runs gets a straight line, and the one who swings for the sky gets the floor under him taken away — the duck, the groin, the knee — because a man who swings that big has already told you where he will be. The gun never enters it: these men are not what the gun is for. Between each he is still and his eyes are already on the next man. He never plays the fight to them; he plays the clock. Afterward the coat, the breath and the draw are the only things he allows himself.
Moment to moment:
— the entrance — he walks and lets five men look at him; his eyes count them and settle on the one who saw him first
— the run — the moment they break, he breaks; eyes on the first man, measuring the range for the leap
— the leap — eyes on the first chest through the air; he lands already looking at the second
— the elbow — the man is inside; the elbow is the shortest thing he has; the eyes are already past him
— the block — he watches the shoulder, not the fist; the forearm and the first body shot are one decision
— the body, the chin — each strike is a fact, not an effort; the face does not change; the eyes stay on the man's centre until the chin
— the bull — he watches the shoulder begin to load and is already moving down the line; the eyes are on the jaw
— the big swing — he watches it wind up and simply is not there; the eyes go to the groin as the fist goes there
— the fold — hands on the neck, knee up; the eyes on the face coming down to meet it
— the fall — he watches the man go over backward the way a man watches a door close
— the stillness — a full second; the eyes travel over the five, checking that each one is done
— the coat — shaken out the way a man shakes rain off it; the eyes on the far end of the corridor already
— the breath, the draw — a man tidying up and taking out what he came with; the eyes never come down to the gun
(Safety: eyes engaged on real targets throughout — the men, the shoulder, the jaw, the groin, the face, the corridor ahead — never glassy; natural blink cadence; the calm is attention, not absence.)

ACTING TASK — GUARD 1, the sweater (the work is in the eyes and the folded arms):
MOTIVE: the others must not see that he is afraid — of the film, of the man, of anything.
GOAL: be one of them.
OBSTACLE: he is the one who admits Dracula scared him, and he is last off the mark, and by the time he arrives four men are on the floor.
TACTIC: arms folded so the hands have nothing to do; a laugh half a beat late; he goes when they go and runs shouting so the shouting will carry him. He arrives last to a corridor full of his own men lying down, and the only thing left to do is swing as big as he can, because a small swing would mean he was afraid — so he shuts his eyes and gives it everything, and the everything goes through empty air. What comes up from below is the last thing on earth he was watching for.
— 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 — to the carpet, then a quick look up: did they laugh? they did; he laughs too
— the turn — his face goes hard because the faces around him do
— the run — last to go, eyes on the backs ahead — and then on the backs on the floor
— the swing — everything he has, wide, eyes half shut for the last of it
— the groin — the eyes fly open and see nothing; the sound is the air leaving; the hands go where the pain is
— the knee — the eyes on the carpet, then the ceiling, then nothing

ACTING TASK — GUARD 2, the hothead (the work is in the eyes and the feet):
MOTIVE: he is right about films and he is right about this corridor, and both need proving.
GOAL: be first to the man.
OBSTACLE: four men who make it a group decision.
TACTIC: he argues the way he fights — the half-step in, the hand up. When the camera comes back to the ring his face is already the first one gone hard, and he is running before the others have finished deciding. He is first, as he wanted, and the last thing he sees is a boot coming at him through the air.
— 「『渇き』見ろよ。」 — the half-step into GUARD 4, eyes hunting for the back-down
— the turn — the first face to change; teeth, the head pushing forward off the neck
— the run — first to go, shouting, eyes on Adam's eyes; the eyes going wide as Adam leaves the ground

ACTING TASK — GUARD 3, the professional (the work is entirely in the eyes):
MOTIVE: he has done this before, and the ones who went down were talking.
GOAL: see it coming.
OBSTACLE: four men making noise in a ring around him, and a man who does what he has never seen done.
TACTIC: he stands at the edge of the ring half-turned and watches the corridor while the others watch each other; he says the one word. He goes low and straight, lets the loud ones arrive first and watches two of them go down in three seconds, and throws his punch clean and hard at the face — the right move against any man he has met before — and finds the man inside his arm.
— the talk — not in it; his eyes on the empty corridor, checking it the way a man checks a lock
— 「おい。」 — flat, to the others, eyes staying on Adam; a report, not an alarm
— the turn — he sinks into his legs while the others make faces
— the run — low, straight, silent; a half-step slower than the loud ones on purpose
— the punch — thrown at the face because that is where the man's eyes are; the forearm is already there

ACTING TASK — GUARD 4, the showman (the work is in the eyes — his crew's eyes as much as Adam's):
MOTIVE: the story of tonight, told later, must have him in it.
GOAL: be looked at.
OBSTACLE: nobody is looking at him for long.
TACTIC: he plays every line across the ring and checks after each whether it landed; when the camera comes back his grin goes hard because the others' faces have, and he runs on the hothead's heels because that is where the picture will be. He arrives a step behind the first man, arms wide for the grab that people see — and gets inside the reach of a man who wanted him there.
— 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」 — across the ring, hand carving the air, eyes going round for agreement
— the laugh at GUARD 1 — head back, then a check: are the others laughing with him
— the turn — the grin hardening late, a flick of the eyes round the ring to match the others
— the run — a step behind the hothead, yelling, arms coming wide
— the elbow — the eyes on Adam's chest a foot away, then on nothing

ACTING TASK — GUARD 5, the bull (the work is in the eyes and the weight):
MOTIVE: he is the one who finishes things; the others are the opening act.
GOAL: be the man who reaches Adam.
OBSTACLE: his own weight — slow to start, impossible to stop — and three men in his way who are down before he gets there.
TACTIC: he takes no part in the film talk; he grunts at it and rolls a shoulder. He does not look at Adam's face; he looks at the middle of the chest, where he is going to put his fist. He goes a beat late and watches three men drop in front of him, and every one of them is fuel: this is his now. He runs flat out, head down, the right shoulder already loading a stride out — and never sees the straight line coming.
— the talk — a grunt; a shoulder rolled; eyes on nothing
— the turn — the growl comes up out of the chest; the eyes fix on Adam's chest and stay there
— the run — a beat late; eyes on the chest through the three men going down; the roar
— the lights go out mid-stride

PHYSICS
The camera is two bare hands and a running, falling body: a fast jitter and a slow lurch in every frame; whips that smear the picture; running strides that slam it; impacts that throw it sideways and let it claw back; a wall clipped with a jolt; a knock from a passing man that spins it; a fall to the carpet that bounces it; and on the floor the trembling and rocking of a man breathing and crawling with a camera in his hands. The horizon swings ten to twenty degrees and is never level. In the slow-motion ramp the shake slows into a wide heaving drift and snaps back with real speed. Five men in a ring argue at five rhythms, turn hard together in one second and break as one wave at five speeds; Adam breaks with them and two runs close twenty metres from both ends. The flying kick: two strides and a launch, the lead knee folding to the chest in the air and the leg pistoning out sideways, heel leading, shoulder and hip stacked in one straight brace behind it — the flat of the boot meets chest and jaw with the whole flying mass behind it, the man leaves his feet, flies two metres straight back folding around the boot and lands flat on his back; Adam comes down on both feet into his stance. The elbow: chest to chest, the arm folds and the point of the elbow travels a short flat arc across the jaw with a few degrees of torso behind it — the head snaps sideways, the legs go, the man drops on his side. The block is a forearm inside the swing knocking the fist a hand's width off its line past the ear; the body shots fold the man around each point of contact — sideways for the hook under the ribs, forward for the straight into the solar plexus, a dip of the knees for the hook to the far ribs — and the straight to the chin snaps the head back and drops him straight down on his back. The slow-motion straight lead lands as the bull's shoulder is still loading a stride out: the straight line beats the curve, the jaw deforms around the knuckles, the head snaps back and up, the run dies under him, his own forward weight doubles the impact, and he falls rigid onto his back with a floor-shaking thud, unconscious. The last man: a wide swing passes through the air where a head was, because the head has dropped a full head's height straight down on folded knees; from the crouch a fist travels one short vertical line up into the groin and lands with a flat thump; every muscle in the struck man locks, the air leaves him in a high breathless sound, both hands clamp between his legs and he folds double, face coming down to waist height; two hands clamp the back of his neck and drag the head down as a knee drives up with the whole rising body behind it — the knee meets the face, the head snaps back and up, the folded body is straightened by the blow, the arms fly out, and he goes over backward stiff and lands flat on his back with a floor-shaking thud, unconscious. The coat, shaken out by both lapels, snaps and falls straight with the weight of heavy black cloth. Skin stays clean on every man; clothes stay whole. The Desert Eagle, drawn at the end, is nearly two kilos: the wrist shows the weight as it comes down out of the coat and it hangs heavy at the thigh, swinging a little with the stride. Adam steps over bodies with the weight of a walking man; the camera crawls after him along the floor.

LIGHTING
Practical only, exactly as @loc_corridor_v1: the sconce wall throws warm hard side-light across the paintings, the ring of men and the carpet, the plain wall falls to shadow, the far end darker than the near; under the shake the sconces smear into short streaks on every whip and jitter as points the rest of the time, and Adam's leap crosses one sconce pool and one shadow. When the lens is close on a face, the near side is lit hard and the far side falls to shadow. In the slow-motion passage the sconce light rakes across the bull's jaw and Adam's knuckles at the moment of contact. From the floor at the end, Adam is a dark figure against the lit ceiling and the row of sconces above him, the side-light catching his jaw and the edge of the coat as it snaps; the drawn pistol picks up a sconce along its slide as it swings down into the low frame.

AUDIO
Ambience: faint bass through the walls from the club, sconce hum, carpet underfoot, five men shifting their weight in a ring, the operator's breathing close to the mic and the constant creak, rustle and knock of the camera in his bare hands throughout — and at the end, the scrape of the camera and his elbows on the carpet.
[Dialogue — spoken in Japanese, natural native delivery, casual, overlapping edges]
0.5–1.7s — GUARD 4: 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」
1.7–2.7s — GUARD 2: 「『渇き』見ろよ。」
2.8–4.0s — GUARD 1: 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 — GUARD 4's short laugh over the end of it; GUARD 5's grunt.
4.7–5.1s — GUARD 3, flat, low: 「おい。」
Nothing else is spoken. GUARD 1 makes one high breathless sound when the groin shot lands — air, not words. Adam says nothing in the scene.
[SFX] Adam's boots on carpet from the far end, walking, then breaking into a run. The turn — five breaths going hard, a growl rising. The break — boots, one shout, then a yell, then a roar, then one more voice, ragged; a body knocking the camera with a thump; the operator's running breath and footfalls under everything from 6.5s to 9.5s; boots hammering carpet at different rhythms from both directions, converging. Two hard steps, a whip of coat in the air, and one flat heavy thump of a boot sole on a chest and jaw, a body flying and landing flat on carpet two metres away; Adam's boots hitting the floor; the camera knocking against the wall. The hard sharp crack of an elbow on a jaw and a body dropping onto its side. The whip of GUARD 3's punch and the slap of a forearm on a forearm; three short body impacts — a deep thud under the ribs, a bark of breath driven out, a thud to the far ribs — and one clean crack of knuckles on a chin, a body dropping flat. The bull's roar and heavy running boots. The ramp: the sound stretches and drops — the roar slowed into a low groan, the air moving ahead of the fist — one deep, dense crack of knuckles on jawbone with a long ring after it — and the sound snaps back to speed as a very heavy body hits the carpet flat on its back, the floor shaking. A shout and the whip of a huge swing through empty air; a flat wet thump low down, and a high thin breathless sound, a whole body locking; two hands slapping onto the back of a neck; the deep crunching thud of a knee meeting a face, and a stiff body going over and slamming flat onto its back. The operator dropping to the floor — knees, elbows, the camera thumping the carpet. Silence with a ring in it, one full second, the operator's breath heaving against the floor. Fabric: heavy black cloth snapped once, hard, and two hands squaring a coat on the shoulders. One long exhale, close, above the mic. Boots on carpet, steady, over and around bodies, walking away; the operator's elbows and knees scraping and thumping after them along the floor, his breath ragged. The coat opening above, and the heavy slide of the Desert Eagle coming down out of it, the weight of it settling at the end of the arm. Boots, the crawl, to the cut. No music.

STYLE
Neo-noir with a dry comic turn, one continuous take from a man's bare hands on a 50 mm: heavy grain, warm sconce light across a gallery of dark paintings, deep shadow, anamorphic ovals and stretched highlights smeared by the shake, the jittering frame, the lurching frame, the running frame, the thrown frame, the frame that falls to the floor and shakes there — never once, in thirty seconds, a frame that holds; the film argument played loose and real, the turn of five faces played in one shaking frame, a man running at five runners and taking the first out of the air; the fight is short straight lines and long stillness — one leap, one knee, and everything else a straight line from the guard — inside a picture that never stops moving, with one speed ramp into a single straight punch as the only ornament, the coat shaken out and the gun drawn seen from the carpet, from where the five are lying.

QUALITY
One unbroken take with no cut anywhere; a heavy, visible handheld shake in every single frame from first to last — jitter and lurch at the calmest, smearing whips and slamming strides and thrown frames in the action, a wide heaving drift in the slow motion, a trembling rocking low frame on the floor at the end; five distinct guards, each matching his man on the sheet, each standing, talking, turning and charging in his own manner; clean Japanese lip sync on the four spoken lines; the five faces turning hard together readable in one frame; the flying kick a single clear arc with the man flying straight back and Adam landing on both feet; the elbow a distinct event dropping a second man; the block, the three body shots and the chin four distinct readable events on one man; the slow-motion straight punch readable through the drift, the jaw deforming and the head snapping back; the duck, the groin shot, the fold, the knee and the backward fall five distinct readable events on the last man; Adam readable from the ground, towering, the coat snapping straight; the pistol appearing only at the end, swinging down into the low frame; consistent frame rate, no ghosting, no duplicated limbs or pistols.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
One continuous handheld take, 30 seconds, one 50 mm lens, one speed ramp at 14.5–16.5s, the camera in the operator's bare hands and shaking hard in every frame of the take — jittering and lurching during the talk, smearing on the whips, slamming with his run, thrown by each impact, clipping the wall once, knocked once by a passing man, heaving in the slow motion, jerked upward with the knee, falling to the carpet at 20.5s and trembling there, crawling after Adam along the floor to the cut — with the horizon swinging ten to twenty degrees and never level. Six people in the scene: Adam and five unarmed guards, everyone's hands empty until the pistol at 26s. The five stand in the middle of the corridor facing each other in a loose ring for the first four and a half seconds and talk in Japanese — four short lines exactly as written, nothing else spoken in the scene; Adam appears at the far end, 20 m away, at 4.5s, walking; the camera whips to him and straight back, and at 5.5–6.5s all five faces turn hard together in one frame and the men break at 6.5s; Adam breaks into a run at the same moment. The camera runs behind the charging men at 6.5–9.5s, reaches the plain wall on Adam's left at 9.5s and stays on Adam's left three-quarter for the fight, drops to the carpet at 20.5s and shoots Adam from the ground, from below, for the coat and the breath, and crawls after him along the floor from 23.5s; every angle a three-quarter or a profile and none of them held. The fight, in this order, one man per event: at 8.5s Adam leaps and his flying boot drives into GUARD 2's chest and jaw — GUARD 2 flies two metres back and lands flat, and Adam lands on both feet; at 10s GUARD 4 arrives inside Adam's reach and Adam's right elbow crosses his jaw — GUARD 4 drops on his side; at 11.5s GUARD 3 throws a right — Adam's left forearm knocks it off its line and he lands three short strikes to the body — hook under the ribs, straight to the solar plexus, hook to the far ribs — and a fourth, a straight lead to the chin, and GUARD 3 drops on his back; at 14.5–16.5s, in slow motion, GUARD 5 runs at Adam and Adam's straight lead lands on his jaw while his shoulder is still loading — GUARD 5 falls rigid onto his back, unconscious; at 17s GUARD 1 swings a huge right — Adam drops under it on folded knees and drives his right fist straight up into GUARD 1's groin, GUARD 1 clamps both hands between his legs and folds double, and Adam's hands drag his head down onto a rising right knee — GUARD 1's head snaps back, his body straightens off the knee and he falls over backward flat on his back, out. All five stay where they fell, clothes whole, skin clean, carpet clean. Adam is completely still in his narrow side-on stance for a full second at 19.5–20.5s while the camera keeps trembling around him; from 20.5s the camera is on the carpet: he shakes his coat out hard by both lapels, squares it on his shoulders and exhales, all seen from the ground and below; then he walks down the corridor over the bodies with the camera crawling and shaking after him along the floor; at 26s, walking, his right hand draws the Desert Eagle from inside the left breast of his coat and it swings down into the low frame and hangs muzzle-down at his thigh to the cut. The pistol is seen only from 26s on and is never fired. Hard cut at 30 on his back and the pistol mid-stride, the frame still shaking on the carpet.

FIGHT STYLE LOCK: this fight has exactly one leap — the flying kick into the first man — and exactly one knee — the rising knee into the last man's face; every other strike travels a short straight line launched from where the hands already rest at guard — the first visible motion of a limb IS the strike itself; between exchanges the fighter is completely still in his narrow side-on stance; the fight is short straight lines and long stillness.

Сцена 3.3 — Плащ і пістолет

Що це дає: тихий фінал для Адама: він поправляє плащ, проходить повз повалених охоронців і дістає пістолет.

Промпт 24· Відео
Seedance 2.521:91080p30 с
SCENE CONTEXT
30 seconds, ONE CONTINUOUS HANDHELD TAKE, shot from the hands of a man who cannot hold a camera still — the frame shakes violently in every single frame, from the first to the last. Hotel corridor, @loc_corridor_v1 — the long gallery corridor hung with framed paintings. Five guards stand in the middle of the corridor facing each other in a loose ring, blocking it, killing a shift with a short argument in Japanese about vampire films, the frame jittering, lurching and tilting around them even now. At the far end Adam walks in, hands empty. One guard sees him; the camera whips down the corridor to Adam in a smear — and whips straight back to the ring, where all five faces have already turned and are going hard, and they break and charge as one wave. Adam charges too. He runs at them and leaves the ground: a flying kick that drives the first man off his feet, and on landing his fist puts the second man's lights out. The third throws a punch; Adam's forearm knocks it off its line and three short strikes go into the body and a fourth into the face, and he folds. The fourth, the biggest, roars and runs — the take ramps into slow motion and Adam's lead fist is already in his face, and he drops. The fifth swings; Adam catches the arm, breaks it at the elbow with a crack, the man screams and drops to his knees, and Adam's fist puts him out. Real speed. Adam goes still — and the operator drops to the carpet among the bodies, so the camera shoots him from the ground, from below, shaking, as he shakes out his coat, squares it on his shoulders and breathes out. He walks on over the bodies and the camera scrambles after him along the floor — and only now his right hand goes inside his coat and comes out with a Desert Eagle, which swings down into the low frame and hangs at his thigh as he walks. Cut. Shot as if by one operator holding the camera in his bare hands with no rig, no support and no rest — running when they run, whipping so hard the image smears, thrown by every impact, clipping the wall, ending up on the floor. Neo-noir with a dry comic turn: the fight is short straight lines and long stillness, and the camera is the one thing in the corridor that never, for a single frame, stops shaking.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@char_adam_video_v1 — VIDEO ELEMENT — ADAM. Face, build, coat, boots, chain 100% match. Face shown throughout, in three-quarter or profile, and from below at the end. Reference controls identity. He fights like a man trained in one thing: a narrow side-on stance, right shoulder and right foot leading, and short straight lines — with one leap in this fight, and everything else straight. His hands are empty throughout; the pistol stays inside his coat until the last five seconds.
@char_corridor_guards_image_v1 — THE GUARDS. A line-up reference: five men from it — the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th and 6th from the left — are the five guards in this corridor, each 100% his man in face, body and clothes. GUARD 1 (1st on the sheet) — the sweater, the one whose arm breaks. GUARD 2 (2nd) — the hothead, the one who takes the flying kick. GUARD 3 (4th) — the professional, the one who takes the body shots. GUARD 4 (5th) — the showman, the one knocked out by the hand on the landing. GUARD 5 (6th) — the bull, the slow-motion one. They are unarmed; their hands are empty from first frame to last. Five men, each appearing once, their skin and clothes clean throughout.
@prop_adam_pistol — ADAM'S PISTOL, a Desert Eagle in .50 Action Express, 100% as the reference — a huge slab of a pistol, nearly two kilos of steel, six-inch barrel, the weight of it visible in the wrist. In this scene it is never fired: it lives inside the left breast of Adam's coat, unseen, until 25s, when his right hand draws it and it hangs muzzle-down at his thigh as he walks out of the scene. The one pistol in the scene.
@loc_corridor_v1 — THE CORRIDOR. Set, materials, light, colour, atmosphere 100% as the reference, including the framed paintings in a row along the sconce wall. About 30 m long here.

LOCATION MAP
A long straight corridor, about 30 m long, 2.5 m wide, 3 m high, carpeted, sconces and framed paintings along one wall at eye level, one painting roughly every 4 m; the opposite wall plain. THE RING: 6 m in from the near end the five stand facing each other across the corridor in a loose ring that blocks it — GUARD 4 and GUARD 2 with their backs toward the painting wall, facing across; GUARD 1 and GUARD 5 opposite them with their backs toward the plain wall; GUARD 3 at the far side of the ring, half-turned so one shoulder faces the group and his eyes have the long empty corridor beyond them. ADAM'S ENTRY: the far end, 20 m from the ring; he walks, then runs, toward the ring with the painting wall on his right and the plain wall on his left. THE COLLISION: about 10 m from the ring, where the two runs meet; the fight happens across the width of the corridor there. THE OPERATOR: starts at the near end, 3 m behind the ring, camera in his bare hands at chest height, runs behind the guards, slides along the plain wall on Adam's left for the fight, drops to the carpet among the bodies at 19s and stays down there, crawling after Adam, to the cut.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
Handheld, camera in two bare hands at chest height, already shaking hard — a fast jitter and a slow lurch on top of it, in the very first frame — 3 m behind the ring at the near end, angled at three-quarter so the ring sits diagonally: GUARD 4's back and shoulder nearest the lens, half-turned toward the others mid-sentence, GUARD 2 across from him with a hand up, GUARD 1 beside GUARD 2 with his arms folded, GUARD 5 huge at the far side of the ring with his arms hanging, GUARD 3 beyond them half-turned, his face toward the empty corridor. Past the ring the corridor runs away 20 m to the far end, empty. The horizon is already ten degrees off and swinging. Exactly five people in the first frame; six in the scene.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous handheld take, 30 seconds, one camera in one man's bare hands, one lens, one speed ramp into slow motion at 13.5–15.5s and back. The shake is the format, and it is heavy: at no point in the thirty seconds does the frame hold for even a quarter of a second. Two layers of it at all times — a fast fine jitter from the hands, and on top of it a slow heavy lurch from the body — and in the action a third: violent whips that smear the image into streaks, running strides that slam the frame up and down, impacts that throw the whole picture sideways and let it claw back. The horizon swings ten to twenty degrees and is never level. In the slow-motion passage the shake slows with the picture into a wide, heaving, tilted drift that never comes to rest; when the speed snaps back so does the full shake. At the end the camera goes down to the carpet and shakes there — the operator's breathing and his hands on the floor making the low frame tremble and rock — and crawls after Adam shaking. There is no still frame in this take.

OPTICS
One lens for the whole take: 50 mm on full frame, about 47° diagonal — a tight lens for a corridor, which magnifies every tremor of the hands into a visible shudder of the whole picture; the operator gets his close-ups by stepping in and his wides by backing to the wall. Anamorphic character: oval bokeh on the sconces, horizontally stretched highlights, gentle barrel curve at the edges, shallow focus that the operator rides by hand and loses — a beat of soft on every fast refocus, focus breathing under the shake, sconces smeared into streaks on every whip.

CAMERA — one unbroken, violently shaking path
0–4.5s: handheld around the outside of the ring, three-quarter, the frame jittering fast and lurching slow the whole time, sliding half a metre in every direction as the operator shifts his feet, tipping toward whoever is speaking and overshooting him, tilting, faces at mid-shot and never centred for long. 4.5–5.5s: a hard whip-pan off GUARD 3's face down the length of the corridor to Adam — the picture smearing into streaks, overshooting him, jerking back past him, jerking back again, shaking — a beat of soft focus snapping sharp on him, small and walking. 5.5–6.5s: a hard whip-pan straight back to the ring, the picture smearing, landing on all five faces at once in one shaking mid-wide frame as they turn and go ugly together. 6.5–8s: the men break past the lens and knock the camera round with them — a real hit, the picture spinning half a turn and finding them — and the operator runs, the frame slamming up and down with every stride, five backs bouncing ahead under the paintings, and beyond them Adam, running at the lens, closing fast. 8–9.5s: still running, the horizon rocking twenty degrees each way, the operator veering to the plain wall and clipping it — a hard jolt — as Adam leaves the ground and the kick and the punch land in a smear of coat; the frame is thrown twice. 9.5–13s: the operator slides along the plain wall to Adam's left three-quarter, full bodies in frame, the camera shaking hard from the run and never calming, thrown on every impact — the block, the three body shots, the face — and clawing back each time. 13–13.5s: a smearing whip to GUARD 5 as he comes. 13.5–15.5s: the take ramps into slow motion, the shake slowing into a wide heaving tilted drift, the lens at chin height swimming after the lead fist into the face. 15.5–18s: real speed, the full shake snapping back; the camera lurches with the caught arm, is thrown by the crack, dips with the man to his knees, thrown again by the last punch. 18–19s: the camera trembles and edges around Adam while he stands still. 19–22s: the operator drops to the carpet — the frame falling, hitting the floor, bouncing — and shoots Adam from the ground, the camera lying on the carpet among the bodies, 15 cm off the floor, tilted up at him, three-quarter from his left and below, his whole figure towering against the ceiling and the sconces, the low frame trembling and rocking with the operator's breathing and his hands on the floor. 22–30s: the camera stays on the ground and crawls after Adam as he walks — 20–30 cm off the carpet, bouncing and shaking with the operator's scramble, the bodies passing in the foreground, Adam's boots and coat hem and the backs of his legs ahead, tilted up enough to hold his back and shoulders, dipping as the pistol swings down into frame at his thigh. Every angle a three-quarter or a profile, and no angle holds for a quarter of a second.

ACTION TIMING — stages of one shaking take

0–4.5s — Five men in a ring, killing a shift, the frame jittering and lurching around them. GUARD 4, back to the painting wall, one hand carving the air at the man across from him: 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」 GUARD 2, facing him, takes a half-step in with a hand up: 「『渇き』見ろよ。」 GUARD 1, beside him, arms folded, admits it to the carpet: 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 GUARD 4 laughs at him across the ring. GUARD 5 grunts, unimpressed by all of them, and rolls a shoulder. GUARD 3, at the far side, is not in it: his head is turned, his eyes on the long empty corridor. The camera shudders, tips from speaker to speaker, overshoots each one, never lands square on any of them.

4.5–5.5s — GUARD 3's head stops. Low, flat, to the others: 「おい。」 The camera whips off his face and down the corridor in a smear, overshoots, jerks back: at the far end, small, Adam has walked in and is walking toward them, hands empty at his sides, coat closed, eyes on the ring, the frame shaking around his small figure.

5.5–6.5s — The camera whips straight back to the ring and lands on all five at once, shaking: five heads already turned down the corridor, and in one second the argument is gone from every face and something else is in them — GUARD 2's head pushing forward off his neck and his teeth showing, GUARD 4's grin gone hard, GUARD 1's jaw clenching, GUARD 5's growl coming up out of his chest as his shoulders roll, GUARD 3 already sinking a centimetre into his legs. One beat of five men going ugly together, and they go.

6.5–8s — They break past the lens as a wave, and one of them knocks the camera: the picture spins half a turn, finds the corridor again, shaking. GUARD 2 out in front, a shout tearing out of him; GUARD 4 a step behind him yelling; GUARD 3 low and straight and silent; GUARD 5 heavy and fast a beat later, roaring; GUARD 1 last, running shouting to keep himself running. The operator runs: five backs strung out down the corridor under the paintings, the frame slamming with every stride — and beyond them Adam has broken into a run too, straight at them, coat flying open behind him, closing the twenty metres from both ends.

8–9.5s — Ten metres from the ring the two runs meet, and Adam leaves the ground. Two strides out he launches — the lead knee folding up to his chest in the air and the leg pistoning out sideways, heel leading, hip and shoulder stacked in one straight brace from shoulder to heel — and the flat of his boot slams into GUARD 2's chest and jaw like stamping a heavy door open. GUARD 2 leaves his feet and flies straight back two metres, folding around the boot, and lands flat on his back and does not get up. Adam comes down out of the kick already turning — his feet hit the carpet in the narrow side-on stance — and GUARD 4 is right there, a step behind the first man, arms wide, and Adam's right fist fires from exactly where the hand has landed at guard, one straight line to the point of the jaw, knuckles vertical, the whole landing weight of his body still travelling down the arm. GUARD 4's head snaps back, his eyes roll, his knees go, and he drops straight down onto the carpet on his back, out before he lands. Two men down in a second and a half; the camera is thrown by the kick, thrown by the punch, clips the plain wall with a jolt and comes back shaking.

9.5–13s — GUARD 3 arrives low and straight and throws a hard right at Adam's head. Adam's left forearm comes up inside the swing and knocks it a hand's width off its line — the fist glancing past his ear — and he is inside the man's arm. Three short strikes into the body, each one a state already landing, the camera shocked harder on each: a short scooping hook digs up under the floating ribs from a palm's width away, knuckles half-turned up, and the man folds sideways around the spot; his rear fist drives straight through into the solar plexus, hips snapping over, and the man's breath leaves him in a bark and his chin drops; his lead arm bends and hooks tight into the ribs on the other side, elbow staying down, torso turning only a few degrees, and the man's knees dip and his hands come off his guard. Then the fourth: his lead fist fires from exactly where it hovers — one straight line to the chin, knuckles vertical, thumb up, elbow unfolding behind the fist, a short glide-step feeding body weight into it. The head snaps back hard, the man's hands leave his body, and he drops straight down onto the carpet on his back and lies still, the frame lurching down after him and back up to Adam. Adam's hand is already back at guard.

13–15.5s — GUARD 5, the bull, has seen it — three men down in five seconds — and it puts fire in him: he roars and comes at Adam flat out, head down, fists up, huge. The operator lunges in, the frame heaving, and at 13.5s the take ramps into slow motion — the shake slowing with it into a wide, heaving, tilted drift — the lens at chin height from Adam's left at three-quarter: the bull is still a stride out, his right shoulder loading — and in that exact instant Adam's lead fist is already landing in the centre of his face, the straight line beating the curve, launched from exactly where the hand rested at guard, knuckles vertical, thumb up, elbow unfolding behind the fist, a long glide-step driving his whole body weight down the line of the arm into the running man. The slow motion holds on the contact while the frame swims: the face deforms around the knuckles, the eyes rolling up, the head snapping back and up so hard the neck arches and the big shoulders follow it, the run dying under him, his own forward weight doubling the hit. His skin stays clean. Adam's face over his own fist: flat, eyes on the point of contact. At 15.5s the take ramps back to real speed and the full shake snaps back: the bull's knees fold and he goes down rigid, straight back, flat on his back on the carpet with a floor-shaking thud that throws the whole frame, arms out, and does not move.

15.5–18s — GUARD 1, the last, arrives shouting and swings a wide right at Adam's head. Adam's hands are already there: his left closes on the wrist as it comes, his right palm slams up under the elbow from below, and he pulls the wrist down as the palm drives the elbow up — the arm bending the wrong way against its own joint with a crack that the camera flinches from. GUARD 1 screams, a raw open-throated scream, the whole body folding around the arm, and his knees hit the carpet in front of Adam, the broken arm hanging, his face at the height of Adam's chest. Adam lets go of the wrist. His right fist comes down one short straight line into the kneeling man's face — and the scream stops. GUARD 1 goes over sideways off his knees and lands on his side on the carpet and lies still. The camera is thrown by the punch.

18–19s — Adam settles back into the narrow side-on stance and goes completely still — feet planted, hands frozen at guard, only his eyes tracking over the lead shoulder across the five men on the floor. The stillness is his alone: the camera trembles, breathes and edges sideways around him for the full second, the frame never resting on him.

19–22s — The operator goes down. The frame drops, hits the carpet, bounces, and comes to lie among the bodies, 15 cm off the floor, tilted up — and there is Adam from the ground: a black figure towering over the lens against the ceiling and the sconces, three-quarter from his left and below, the fallen men's shoulders and boots in the foreground of the low frame, the whole picture trembling and rocking with the operator's breathing on the floor. His hands come down. He takes the coat by both lapels and shakes it out — one hard shake, the black cloth snapping and falling straight — and squares it on his shoulders with one tug and settles the collar, seen from below, huge. One long breath out through the mouth, the shoulders dropping with it, the breath visible in the chest from down here.

22–30s — He walks — the same pace he came in with — on down the corridor over the bodies toward where the ring stood, and the camera stays on the ground and scrambles after him: 20–30 cm off the carpet, bouncing hard with the operator's crawl, the fallen men sliding past in the foreground — the sweater on his side with the arm under him, the bull's outflung arm, the professional flat, the showman flat, the hothead flat on his back — Adam's boots and the swinging hem of the coat and the backs of his legs ahead, the frame tilted up enough to hold his back and shoulders, everything shaking. And as he walks, at 25s, his right hand goes up inside the left breast of his coat — above the low frame — and comes back down with the Desert Eagle, the big pistol swinging down into the picture and hanging at his thigh, muzzle down, moving a little with his stride, huge in the low frame, the camera jolting after it along the floor, the paintings and sconces juddering past high above. Hard cut at 30 on his back and the pistol at his side mid-stride, the frame still shaking on the carpet.

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken — all six play it): make it look like nothing. Five men stand in a ring in the middle of a corridor arguing about films because a man at the end of it is nothing; when he turns out to be something they go at him five on one because that is still nothing. Adam plays the same line from his end — he runs at five men because waiting would mean they were something, the fight is a chore, the coat gets shaken out afterward because nothing happened, and the gun comes out only when the corridor is his, for whoever is behind the door. The event is the moment "nothing" turns out to be a very expensive word, and it ends with the one man who never dropped the line walking away down the corridor with the thing he came to use — seen from the floor, where everyone else is.

ACTING TASK — ADAM (fully invested; the work is in his eyes and his stillness):
MOTIVE (his fuel): a man to see at the end of this corridor and a clock running.
GOAL: get past five men spending as little time as possible — and keep the gun for the one who deserves it.
OBSTACLE: five men who want him to stop walking, and a body that wants to enjoy this — the fighter in him wants the bull, and letting him have it costs time.
TACTIC: when they run he runs, because the fastest way through five men is into them, and the first two are close enough together to be one problem — a boot for one and the landing for the other. After that each man gets exactly what he brings: the one who punches gets a forearm and the body opened up, the one who runs gets a straight line, the one who swings wide gets his arm. The gun never enters it: these men are not what the gun is for. Between each he is still and his eyes are already on the next man. He never plays the fight to them; he plays the clock. Afterward the coat, the breath and the draw are the only things he allows himself.
Moment to moment:
— the entrance — he walks and lets five men look at him; his eyes count them and settle on the one who saw him first
— the run — the moment they break, he breaks; eyes on the first two, measuring the gap between them
— the leap — eyes on the first chest through the air, and already on the second jaw before the boot has landed
— the block — he watches the shoulder, not the fist; the forearm and the first body shot are one decision
— the body, the chin — each strike is a fact, not an effort; the face does not change; the eyes stay on the man's centre until the chin
— the bull — he watches the shoulder begin to load and is already moving down the line; the eyes are on the face
— the arm — he watches the wide swing come and takes it the way a man takes a coat off a hook; the crack is a fact
— the kneeling man — one short line down; the eyes leave him before he has finished falling
— the stillness — a full second; the eyes travel over the five, checking that each one is done
— the coat — shaken out the way a man shakes rain off it; the eyes on the far end of the corridor already
— the breath, the draw — a man tidying up and taking out what he came with; the eyes never come down to the gun
(Safety: eyes engaged on real targets throughout — the men, the shoulder, the face, the arm, the corridor ahead — never glassy; natural blink cadence; the calm is attention, not absence.)

ACTING TASK — GUARD 1, the sweater (the work is in the eyes and the folded arms):
MOTIVE: the others must not see that he is afraid — of the film, of the man, of anything.
GOAL: be one of them.
OBSTACLE: he is the one who admits Dracula scared him, and he is last off the mark, and by the time he arrives four men are on the floor.
TACTIC: arms folded so the hands have nothing to do; a laugh half a beat late; he goes when they go and runs shouting so the shouting will carry him. He arrives last to a corridor full of his own men lying down, and the only thing left to do is swing as big as he can, because a small swing would mean he was afraid. The scream is the first honest sound he has made all night.
— 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 — to the carpet, then a quick look up: did they laugh? they did; he laughs too
— the turn — his face goes hard because the faces around him do
— the run — last to go, eyes on the backs ahead — and then on the backs on the floor
— the swing — everything he has, wide, eyes shut for the last of it
— the arm — the scream; the eyes on his own elbow, then up at the fist, then nothing

ACTING TASK — GUARD 2, the hothead (the work is in the eyes and the feet):
MOTIVE: he is right about films and he is right about this corridor, and both need proving.
GOAL: be first to the man.
OBSTACLE: four men who make it a group decision.
TACTIC: he argues the way he fights — the half-step in, the hand up. When the camera comes back to the ring his face is already the first one gone hard, and he is running before the others have finished deciding. He is first, as he wanted, and the last thing he sees is a boot coming at him through the air.
— 「『渇き』見ろよ。」 — the half-step into GUARD 4, eyes hunting for the back-down
— the turn — the first face to change; teeth, the head pushing forward off the neck
— the run — first to go, shouting, eyes on Adam's eyes; the eyes going wide as Adam leaves the ground

ACTING TASK — GUARD 3, the professional (the work is entirely in the eyes):
MOTIVE: he has done this before, and the ones who went down were talking.
GOAL: see it coming.
OBSTACLE: four men making noise in a ring around him, and a man who does what he has never seen done.
TACTIC: he stands at the edge of the ring half-turned and watches the corridor while the others watch each other; he says the one word. He goes low and straight, lets the loud ones arrive first and watches two of them go down in one leap, and throws his punch clean and hard at the face — the right move against any man he has met before — and finds the man inside his arm.
— the talk — not in it; his eyes on the empty corridor, checking it the way a man checks a lock
— 「おい。」 — flat, to the others, eyes staying on Adam; a report, not an alarm
— the turn — he sinks into his legs while the others make faces
— the run — low, straight, silent; a half-step slower than the loud ones on purpose
— the punch — thrown at the face because that is where the man's eyes are; the forearm is already there

ACTING TASK — GUARD 4, the showman (the work is in the eyes — his crew's eyes as much as Adam's):
MOTIVE: the story of tonight, told later, must have him in it.
GOAL: be looked at.
OBSTACLE: nobody is looking at him for long.
TACTIC: he plays every line across the ring and checks after each whether it landed; when the camera comes back his grin goes hard because the others' faces have, and he runs on the hothead's heels because that is where the picture will be. He arrives a step behind the first man, arms wide for the grab that people see — and the first man is already in the air past him and the fist is already on his own jaw.
— 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」 — across the ring, hand carving the air, eyes going round for agreement
— the laugh at GUARD 1 — head back, then a check: are the others laughing with him
— the turn — the grin hardening late, a flick of the eyes round the ring to match the others
— the run — a step behind the hothead, yelling, arms coming wide
— the landing — the eyes on the boot going past him, then on nothing

ACTING TASK — GUARD 5, the bull (the work is in the eyes and the weight):
MOTIVE: he is the one who finishes things; the others are the opening act.
GOAL: be the man who reaches Adam.
OBSTACLE: his own weight — slow to start, impossible to stop — and three men in his way who are down before he gets there.
TACTIC: he takes no part in the film talk; he grunts at it and rolls a shoulder. He does not look at Adam's face; he looks at the middle of the chest, where he is going to put his fist. He goes a beat late and watches three men drop in front of him, and every one of them is fuel: this is his now. He runs flat out, head down, the right shoulder already loading a stride out — and never sees the straight line coming.
— the talk — a grunt; a shoulder rolled; eyes on nothing
— the turn — the growl comes up out of the chest; the eyes fix on Adam's chest and stay there
— the run — a beat late; eyes on the chest through the three men going down; the roar
— the lights go out mid-stride

PHYSICS
The camera is two bare hands and a running, falling body: a fast jitter and a slow lurch in every frame; whips that smear the picture; running strides that slam it; impacts that throw it sideways and let it claw back; a wall clipped with a jolt; a knock from a passing man that spins it; a fall to the carpet that bounces it; and on the floor the trembling and rocking of a man breathing and crawling with a camera in his hands. The horizon swings ten to twenty degrees and is never level. In the slow-motion ramp the shake slows into a wide heaving drift and snaps back with real speed. Five men in a ring argue at five rhythms, turn hard together in one second and break as one wave at five speeds; Adam breaks with them and two runs close twenty metres from both ends. The flying kick: two strides and a launch, the lead knee folding to the chest in the air and the leg pistoning out sideways, heel leading, shoulder and hip stacked in one straight brace behind it — the flat of the boot meets chest and jaw with the whole flying mass behind it, the man leaves his feet, flies two metres straight back folding around the boot and lands flat on his back; Adam comes down into his stance and the landing weight goes straight down his right arm into the second man's jaw — one short straight line, the head snaps back, the knees go, the man drops straight down on his back. The block is a forearm inside the swing knocking the fist a hand's width off its line past the ear; the body shots fold the man around each point of contact — sideways for the hook under the ribs, forward for the straight into the solar plexus, a dip of the knees for the hook to the far ribs — and the straight to the chin snaps the head back and drops him straight down on his back. The slow-motion straight lead lands as the bull's shoulder is still loading a stride out: the straight line beats the curve, the face deforms around the knuckles, the head snaps back and up, the run dies under him, his own forward weight doubles the impact, and he falls rigid onto his back with a floor-shaking thud, unconscious. The arm: a wrist caught in one hand as the swing comes, a palm slammed up under the elbow with the other, the wrist pulled down as the elbow is driven up — the joint bends against itself and gives with a crack, the body folds around the arm, the knees hit the carpet, a scream — and one short straight punch down into the kneeling face ends it, the man going over sideways off his knees. The coat, shaken out by both lapels, snaps and falls straight with the weight of heavy black cloth. Skin stays clean on every man; clothes stay whole. The Desert Eagle, drawn at the end, is nearly two kilos: the wrist shows the weight as it comes down out of the coat and it hangs heavy at the thigh, swinging a little with the stride. Adam steps over bodies with the weight of a walking man; the camera crawls after him along the floor.

LIGHTING
Practical only, exactly as @loc_corridor_v1: the sconce wall throws warm hard side-light across the paintings, the ring of men and the carpet, the plain wall falls to shadow, the far end darker than the near; under the shake the sconces smear into short streaks on every whip and jitter as points the rest of the time, and Adam's leap crosses one sconce pool and one shadow. When the lens is close on a face, the near side is lit hard and the far side falls to shadow. In the slow-motion passage the sconce light rakes across the bull's face and Adam's knuckles at the moment of contact. From the floor at the end, Adam is a dark figure against the lit ceiling and the row of sconces above him, the side-light catching his jaw and the edge of the coat as it snaps; the drawn pistol picks up a sconce along its slide as it swings down into the low frame.

AUDIO
Ambience: faint bass through the walls from the club, sconce hum, carpet underfoot, five men shifting their weight in a ring, the operator's breathing close to the mic and the constant creak, rustle and knock of the camera in his bare hands throughout — and at the end, the scrape of the camera and his elbows on the carpet.
[Dialogue — spoken in Japanese, natural native delivery, casual, overlapping edges]
0.5–1.7s — GUARD 4: 「ブレイドが最強だろ。」
1.7–2.7s — GUARD 2: 「『渇き』見ろよ。」
2.8–4.0s — GUARD 1: 「…ドラキュラ、怖かった。」 — GUARD 4's short laugh over the end of it; GUARD 5's grunt.
4.7–5.1s — GUARD 3, flat, low: 「おい。」
Nothing else is spoken. GUARD 1 screams when his arm breaks — a raw sound, no words. Adam says nothing in the scene.
[SFX] Adam's boots on carpet from the far end, walking, then breaking into a run. The turn — five breaths going hard, a growl rising. SCENE CONTEXT
ALLERGIC — VICTOR'S OFFICE — PART A: THE LINE.
The film OPENS on the impact: Adam kicks the double door open and walks in. He has come for Victor over Kenny's death — not to argue, to carry out a sentence already passed. He HATES this man, he wants him dead, and the hatred is visible from the first step: in the eyes, in the locked jaw, in the pressure of every word. It GROWS through the scene — the voice stays low in pitch and never becomes a shout, but it is hard, heavy and loaded, the hatred thickening sentence by sentence; he never loses control. On the last sentence of his verdict the hatred bares its teeth as he raises the gun: a restrained snarl of PURE ANGER at full boil — no smile in it, no smirk, no enjoyment anywhere in the face — a decision, not a loss of control.
Victor receives him as a cunning, smirking host — the fox who knows exactly why the guest has come and savors it. He answers the verdict with hysterical laughter — and then, mid-breath, his own mask drops: the laughter CURDLES into honest IRRITATION and rising anger — it INFURIATES him that Adam runs errands for pathetic little humans instead of standing at Victor's side. He crushes out his cigar, rises sharply, and throws his claim at Adam with a pointing finger.
The pass ends on standing Victor, finger aimed at Adam, the claim just spoken. Victor remains human throughout.
DIALOGUE — VERBATIM AND COMPLETE
Exactly FIVE spoken lines, English, each spoken once, word for word, TO ITS LAST WORD — no line shortened, swallowed or cut off by an edit or an impact; if timing drifts, the words win. Nothing else is spoken by anyone; Victor's laugh has no words in it.
L1 — VICTOR: "Oh, Adam. I've been waiting for you. Sit down. Have a drink." — sly, smirking, honeyed; complete only when "…drink." is heard.
L2 — ADAM: "Kenny's gone." — spoken AS his eyes travel up from the offered drink to Victor; low in pitch and HARD, pushed through clenched teeth, heavy with hatred — not a whisper; only a breath-short beat between the two words; complete only when "…gone." is heard.
L3 — ADAM: "There's a line, Victor. You knew exactly where it was. You stepped over it anyway. Now it's time to pay." — four short sentences separated by held pauses, and the HATRED BUILDS through them: each sentence lands harder, heavier and more dangerous than the one before, the gravel thickening, the consonants bitten; the voice stays low in pitch and never becomes a shout, but it is never quiet — dense, pressured, filling the room; the final sentence is the MOST CHARGED speech of the film: the hatred at FULL BOIL, pressed to the very edge of a shout without ever crossing it, a live growl riding under every word, each word torn off separately through a restrained snarl of PURE ANGER — the teeth bared in fury, NEVER in a smile: no smirk, no grin, no amusement anywhere in his face — a half-beat hold before "pay." and the word dropped like an axe, carrying the plain intent to end Victor; complete only when "…pay." is heard.
L4 — VICTOR: "Still running errands for those sad little people?" — the tone RAISED in IRRITATION and contempt, the first raised voice of the film: the laughter has curdled — it INFURIATES him that the boy serves those pathetic little people — hard and biting, never a shriek; complete only when "…people?" is heard.
L5 — VICTOR: "You're one of us, kid. Always were." — angry, hard, bitten — an affirmation thrown at Adam like an accusation, punctuated by the pointing finger; complete only when "…Always were." is heard.
A hard cut is a cut of PICTURE ONLY: a line begun continues across it unbroken, no pause, no restart, no repeated word. On-screen non-speakers keep their lips still.
STYLE
Photorealistic live-action confrontation. Dark practical light, tactile surfaces, physical weight and emotionally specific, naturalistic performances — real breath, real saliva in the laugh, real muscle in every turn of the face.
30 seconds. Five shots, hard cuts only — and ONE CAMERA IDEA carried through all five: THE VICE. Every shot of this film MOVES INWARD — a slow, deliberate convergence on the men, never away from them, and the speed of that convergence grows as the scene heats: a glacial push from behind the waiting host (SHOT 1), a lateral glide along the duel (SHOT 2), a low creep over the host's head into the guest's face (SHOT 3), a slow arc that closes around the executioner as his verdict lands (SHOT 4), and a slow drive over the levelled gun into the breaking host (SHOT 5). The audience is walked, shot by shot, closer to the point of no return.
The tension comes from a duel of composure: one man filling with hatred that never once becomes a shout — the audience hears it in the hard, heavy voice and sees it in his eyes and jaw, until it bares its teeth in pure anger on the last sentence of the verdict — and the other laughing it off, until HIS composure is the one that snaps, loudly.
